papers.title: Analysis and Simulation of Cooperative Buffer Strategies for Traffic Wave Mitigation
papers.summary: Stop-and-go waves in traffic flow pose a persistent challenge, compromising safety, efficiency, and environmental sustainability. This paper presents a novel mitigation strategy identified through an exploratory multi-agent deep reinforcement learning experiment in a ring-road environment. In this experiment, the agents are observed to develop a driving policy in which most vehicles maintain minimal headways to maximize throughput, while a single "buffer" vehicle adopts a larger headway to absorb perturbations and prevent wave propagation. We demonstrate within a parametrised analytical framework, under a linearized long-wavelength string-stability criterion, that this strategy optimises overall flow among non-uniform time-gap distributions. We further show through simulation that adapting this cooperative strategy to classical nonlinear car-following models, such as the Intelligent Driver and Full Velocity Difference models, yields improvements in stability, traffic efficiency, and speed oscillation across broad parameter sweeps. We additionally show that sharing the buffering role among multiple vehicles reduces the per-vehicle buffering time and mitigates intra-platoon instabilities in larger platoons, which may offer a more practically feasible strategy.

papers.title: Fairness, Travel, and Market Potential: An Optimization Framework for NBA Expansion
papers.summary: The potential expansion of the National Basketball Association (NBA) to 32 teams raises the question of how to restructure its conferences and divisions while balancing travel efficiency, fairness in team travel burdens, and commercial exposure. This study provides a quantitative framework for expansion planning. We develop two optimization models: one minimizing total travel distance and another following the Kalai-Smorodinsky (KS) proportional-improvement principle. The KS model maximizes the smallest normalized travel improvement between a team's fixed reference and individual ideal. Both models incorporate an opponent-exposure constraint to account for commercial considerations, and take into account road trips when measuring travel distance. Using data from all 30 current franchises and six candidate cities (Seattle, Las Vegas, Montreal, Vancouver, Tampa, and Mexico City), we evaluate 15 pairwise expansion scenarios under alternative season lengths and divisional formats. In the 30-team comparison, KS strikes a good balance between overall travel efficiency and fairness across teams, giving greater attention to individual travel burdens while keeping total travel close to the distance-minimizing solution. The expansion results show that travel requirements depend jointly on the candidate city pair and the competition format, highlighting the need to assess expansion and realignment together. Our study offers a flexible decision support framework for league executives, policymakers, and sports economists. It makes the trade-offs between total travel, individual gains, and opponent exposure explicit, providing evidence-based guidance for strategic league design.

papers.title: Effect of Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Material Properties on Simulated Transcatheter Pulmonary Placement
papers.summary: FE simulations emulating TPV system deployment in patient-specific right ventricular outflow tracts (RVOT) assume material properties for the RVOT and adjacent tissues. Sensitivity of the deployment to variation in RVOT material properties is unknown. Moreover, the effect of a transannular patch stiffness and location on simulated TPV deployment has not been explored. A sensitivity analysis on the material properties of a patient-specific RVOT during TPV deployment, modeled as an uncoupled HGO material, was conducted using FEBioUncertainSCI. Further, the effects of a transannular patch during TPV deployment were analyzed by considering two patch locations and four patch stiffnesses. Visualization of results and quantification were performed using custom metrics implemented in SlicerHeart and FEBio. Sensitivity analysis revealed that the shear modulus of the ground matrix (c), fiber modulus (k1), fiber dispersion (kappa), and fiber mean orientation angle (gamma) had the greatest effect on 95th%ile stress, whereas only c had the greatest effect on 95th%ile Lagrangian strain. First-order sensitivity indices contributed the greatest to the total-order sensitivity indices. Simulations using a transannular patch revealed that peak stress and strain were dependent on patch location and the underlying vessel geometry, with increasing patch stiffness modulating the magnitude of local stress concentrations. As stiffness of the patch increased, greater stress was observed at the interface connecting the patch to the RVOT, and stress in the patch itself increased while strain decreased. The total enclosed volume by the TPV device remained unchanged across all simulated patch cases. This study highlights that while uncertainties in tissue material properties and patch locations may influence functional outcomes, FE simulations provide a reliable framework for evaluating these outcomes in TPVR.

papers.title: Learning relaxation time distributions from spectral induced polarization data with a complex-valued variational autoencoder
papers.summary: Spectral induced polarization (SIP) is a geophysical method used to characterize subsurface materials. It measures the frequency-dependent complex electrical resistivity of rocks and soils through the application of an alternating current. Debye and Warburg decompositions are standard methods for analyzing and interpreting SIP data, as they allow estimation of the relaxation time distribution (RTD) of geomaterials. However, conventional decomposition approaches treat measurements independently, work in real-valued spaces despite the complex-valued nature of SIP data, and provide limited uncertainty quantification. These limitations reduce the effectiveness of conventional decomposition on heterogeneous datasets. We reformulate the decomposition approach as an unsupervised machine learning problem and introduce a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) that learns a shared mapping from SIP datasets to continuous RTDs. The model is validated on a dataset comprising 140 laboratory and field SIP measurements of granular mixtures, sedimentary and igneous rock, and cementitious materials. The CVAE operates in complex-valued data space and achieves reconstruction errors of 0.53 % and 0.27 % for the imaginary and phase components of resistivity, respectively, with evidence of improvement over conventional methods at corresponding p-values of 0.007 and 0.06. The inferred RTDs are stable and physically consistent, and their total chargeability and mean relaxation time correlate with polarizable grain content and grain size, respectively, with coefficients of determination up to 0.98. An additional contribution of the proposed method is the learned latent representation, which organizes SIP spectra into a structured space. Unsupervised clustering in a two-dimensional projection of this space improves the silhouette score by nearly a factor of two relative to conventional RTD parameters.

papers.title: Framework for atom-resolved decomposition of second-harmonic generation in nonlinear optical crystals
papers.summary: In this work, we develop a new framework for computing atom-resolved contributions to optical properties based on atoms-in-molecules (AIM) schemes. The formalism is independent of the specific AIM method and is made rigorous by partitioning momentum matrix elements into atomic contributions while exactly satisfying the relevant sum rules. Zincblende GaP provides a two-atom demonstration of the atom-resolved second-harmonic-generation (SHG) analysis using five AIM partitioning methods. The two-center Ga--P channels account for $80.6$--$82.2\%$ of the SHG response, despite the pronounced partition dependence of the atomic charges. We then apply the framework to six representative ultraviolet nonlinear-optical crystals: $\beta$-BaB$_2$O$_4$ (BBO), LiB$_3$O$_5$ (LBO), CsB$_3$O$_5$ (CBO), CsLiB$_6$O$_{10}$ (CLBO), KBe$_2$BO$_3$F$_2$ (KBBF), and LiCs$_2$PO$_4$ (LCPO). The atom-triplet decomposition shows that two-center channels dominate the principal SHG components, while on-site terms are smaller and multicenter terms provide an important secondary contribution. Although the AIM charges, detailed local percentages, and exact pathway ranks depend on the partition, the physical interpretation remains stable across the tested AIM methods. B/O-only pathways dominate the leading responses of KBBF and LBO. Mixed pathways involving B/O or P/O atoms and cations make substantial contributions to the leading responses of BBO, CBO, CLBO, and LCPO. The decomposition framework therefore establishes a quantitative connection between local response pathways and the bulk nonlinear-optical response.

papers.title: Performance Evaluation of Straw Tubes with Muon Beams at CERN
papers.summary: We present results from two test beam campaigns that investigate the performance of straw tube detectors as potential candidates for an FCC-ee straw tracker. These studies were carried out at CERN using 150 GeV muon beams. Dedicated algorithms were developed to determine both single tube spatial resolution for the primary coordinate in the $r-\phi$ plane and spatial resolution for the secondary coordinate along the tube direction within a straw chamber. Detection efficiency was also evaluated as a function of the extrapolated hit position for each tube. Both datasets showed consistent results for spatial resolutions and efficiency. The average single-tube spatial resolution in the primary $r-\phi$ coordinate is approximately 110 $\mu$m, while the average spatial resolution in the secondary coordinate along the tube direction is approximately 2 mm. Most tubes show a single-tube detection efficiency above 98%.

papers.title: Lacunarity in a Two-Dimensional Atomizing Liquid Jet
papers.summary: Atomization stretches and folds the liquid--gas interface before fragmenting it into ligaments and droplets, making fractal measures a natural descriptor of the lacunarity of the final breakup state. We examine this idea in two-dimensional (2D) VOF-DNS of a liquid jet with adaptive mesh refinement in Basilisk. Box-counting of the full resolved interface does not yield a single scale-independent exponent. Instead, two scaling ranges appear, separated by a crossover near the box-counting level \(L_{\mathrm{box}}\simeq7\): coarser boxes measure the folded connected jet envelope, whereas finer boxes increasingly sample ligaments, droplets, and nearly smooth local interface segments. Decomposing the interface into detached droplets, ligaments, and the connected main body shows that the relevant effective dimension is structure dependent. Droplets are most lacunar with dimension below one, ligaments occupy an intermediate level, and the main body carries the largest coarse-scale dimension. This hierarchy persists over $Re_l=100$--$10^4$ at fixed $\We_g=200$. The lacunarity of droplets is reminiscent of that of the object positions in the night sky hypothesized by de Vaucouleurs.

papers.title: Quantum analysis of a multi-frequency laser with a photonic time crystal
papers.summary: The present study considers the operation of a laser that incorporates a photonic time crystal (PTC), the purpose of which is to generate a field characterised by multiple widely separated optical frequencies. This laser is the subject of both a proposal and theoretical investigation. The laser comprises an active medium and a PTC within a small cavity constructed from two photonic crystals that are positioned in an overlapping configuration. PTC is modulated by an external field. The spikes in the laser field spectrum are separated by the PTC modulation frequency. The development of a quantum model of the laser with PTC has been achieved, and the analysis of a lasing mode with multi-frequency spikes has been made. The investigation focused on the study of lasing conditions, output power, and the lasing field spectra. The experimental realization of the multi-frequency laser with PTC under realistic conditions is discussed.

papers.title: Sparse Contextual Coupling Reshapes Diffusion Geometry in Multilayer Hypergraphs
papers.summary: Many complex systems combine dense background structure with sparse contextual information. We introduce a diffusion-based framework for analyzing how sparse condition-specific layers reshape diffusion geometry in multilayer hypergraphs. Each layer is represented as a weighted hypergraph, layers are coupled through shared entities, and random walks on the coupled system induce multiscale diffusion distances between nodes. We apply the framework to disease-conditioned gene networks by coupling a dense MSigDB functional gene-set layer to sparse disease-specific DGIdb drug-gene hypergraphs, with disease-associated drugs selected from DDDB and HumanNet-GSP used to define external gene weights. Across Bipolar Disorder, Schizophrenia, Leukemia, and Breast Cancer, the disease-specific layer contains less than 2 percent of genes in the coupled system, yet substantially changes diffusion distances and community structure. Centrality analysis suggests that this disproportionate effect arises because DGIdb-associated genes occupy influential positions in the MSigDB-derived functional network. The resulting diffusion-derived communities are stable under subsampling and show coherent post hoc functional enrichment, including signaling and neurotransmission categories in neuropsychiatric diseases and immune, translational, and metabolic categories in cancer-associated diseases. Community-level comparisons further reveal disease similarities not reducible to direct DGIdb gene overlap, including a Breast Cancer-Schizophrenia relationship consistent with recent biomedical evidence. These results show that sparse contextual layers can induce interpretable nonlocal changes in higher-order network geometry.

papers.title: Linear causality and stability constraints on relativistic second-order magnetohydrodynamics
papers.summary: In this work, we construct a theoretical framework for relativistic second-order magnetohydrodynamics based on entropy current analysis. The formalism consistently incorporates finite relaxation dynamics of the dissipative fluxes, providing a transient framework suitable for analyzing linear stability and short-wavelength causality. Utilizing linear mode analysis, we investigate the constraints imposed by causality and stability on this anisotropic system. By linearizing the theory around a homogeneous equilibrium state, we identify the magnetosonic, Alfv\'en, and charge-diffusion sectors, together with their coupling terms. For each sector, we derive asymptotic dispersion relations in both the long-wavelength (small-$k$) and short-wavelength (large-$k$) regimes, validating them against exact numerical roots. Our numerical analysis confirms the accuracy of these asymptotic solutions and uncovers a nontrivial angular dependence, especially near special propagation directions where the ordinary momentum expansion becomes less reliable. By evaluating the large-$k$ behavior of the propagating branches alongside the damping properties of non-hydrodynamic modes, we delineate the corresponding causality constraints. We find that the admissible linear causal domain is governed by the interplay between propagation direction, anisotropic transport coefficients, and relaxation times, with the resulting bounds being intrinsically mode-dependent. These findings provide a systematic theoretical basis for investigating linear stability and short-wavelength causality in relativistic magnetohydrodynamics beyond the first-order approximation.

papers.title: Full Characterization of a Mock Nuclear Waste Barrel with Muon Tomography using Micromegas Detectors
papers.summary: Muon tomography based on multiple Coulomb scattering provides a non-destructive method to image dense and shielded objects using naturally occurring cosmic-ray muons. In the context of nuclear waste characterization, we present the experimental imaging of a 205-L mock waste barrel using a dedicated 1m$^2$ muon scattering tomography test bench. The system employs multiplexed resistive Micromegas detectors, enabling stable and high-precision muon tracking. Monte Carlo simulations are first used to characterize material-dependent scattering signatures and to quantitatively assess identification performance using statistical reconstruction. These simulation-based results are then used to define objective discrimination thresholds, which are subsequently applied to experimental data for the localization and identification of internal anomalies. Using an Angle Statistics Reconstruction algorithm, we achieve a spatial resolution of 10 mm and demonstrate the three-dimensional imaging of an internal structure containing both low- and high-radiation length materials. Material discrimination performance is evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis, yielding high identification efficiency for dense metallic inclusions such as lead and steel (AUC $\geq$ 0.96) within acquisition times of a few days, while cavities also exhibit strong contrast. Experimental results show good agreement with detailed Monte Carlo simulations. By establishing a continuous workflow from simulation-based performance characterization to practical application on measured data, this work provides a quantitatively validated framework for muon scattering tomography applied to complex, shielded objects.

papers.title: Optical chirality of membrane metasurfaces with broken in-plane symmetry
papers.summary: We study chiroptical properties of single-layer dielectric membrane metasurfaces with broken in-plane symmetry. Although chiral optics was long tied to structures lacking any mirror symmetry, planar (2D) chiral structures that retain a horizontal mirror plane now attract growing attention for their strong chiral optical effects. We explicitly show and explain how single-layer metasurfaces can achieve strong resonant chiral response. Although the single-layer geometry forbids conventional co-polarized circular dichroism, strong resonant conversion circular dichroism appears to be possible in particular wavelength ranges determined by the spectra of photonic eigenmodes. We explore its origin starting with a $C_4$ rotation-symmetric and in-plane mirror-symmetric membrane metasurface and applying to it various in-plane perturbations. Simultaneous breaking of the in-plane mirror symmetry and lifting the rotation symmetry unlocks resonantly enhanced circular conversion dichroism. We derive selection rules for this effect and trace its origin to eigenmode interference and intercoupling using chiral coupled-mode theory. Material absorption weakens the conversion dichroism produced by modes of opposite up-down parity, but it is essential for that produced by modes of the same parity.

papers.title: Beam shifts and eigenpolarisations for the reflection of vortex beams from homogeneous magnetic surfaces
papers.summary: Probing surfaces with optical beams is a powerful technique utilised for material characterisation, and more recently, measuring surface magnetisation with vortex beams has opened new avenues by utilising OAM beams for metrology. In this paper, we focus on extending the theoretical framework of unit order vortex beam reflection to spatially homogeneous magnetic surfaces, and derive expressions for the Goos-H\"anchen (GH) and Imbert-Federov (IF) shifts. We calculate closed form expressions for the plane wave eigenpolarisations, polarisations which remain in the same vectorial direction after reflection, for both dielectric and homogeneous magnetic surfaces. These are found by extending the singularimetry formalism for dielectric surfaces, where the position of the phase vortex can be analytically approximated by taking into account the finite beam width, to homogeneous magnetic surfaces. From this we find the eigenpolarisations of the unit order vortex beam for reflection from both dielectric and homogeneous magnetic surfaces. We discuss with relation to the analytical forms of the Jones matrices for GH and IF shifts the additional reflection behaviour observed for homogeneous magnetic surfaces.

papers.title: Modeling inhomogeneous spatial point configurations with applications to replicated patterns in real-life waiting crowds
papers.summary: In this article, we connect statistical inference for spatial point processes with the analysis of waiting pedestrian crowds through two interconnected contributions. First, on the methodological side we develop an inference procedure for semiparametric spatial point process models leveraging replicated spatial patterns, i.e., multiple approximately independent realizations from the same process. Second, we show that spatial point processes provide a suitable modeling framework for waiting pedestrians, capturing two key aspects: spatial inhomogeneity driven by location attractiveness and repulsive interactions between pedestrians. These two components are central to the inference problem itself, since spatial point process modeling hinges on disentangling background intensity from interaction. Although replicated spatial patterns are rare in point process literature, they are available here through a unique real-life pedestrian dataset, thereby directly linking the methodological development to the physical application. We use the proposed methods to fit and evaluate determinantal and Gibbs point processes in a simulation study and a real-world case study. Despite persistent challenges in decoupling the influences of inhomogeneity from interaction, these models are able to reproduce key empirical features of waiting pedestrians.

papers.title: When is vaccine prioritization worth optimizing?
papers.summary: Optimizing vaccine prioritization is often treated as the default policy response when vaccine supply is limited. Yet optimized prioritization carries administrative, ethical and communication costs, motivating an upstream question: whether differences among vaccine allocations can alter epidemic outcomes enough to make optimization epidemiologically necessary. We show that optimization is not always worth pursuing: in some regimes, vaccination markedly reduces epidemic burden, but many feasible allocation rules perform almost equally well, making the necessity of optimization low. We quantify this necessity as the range of epidemic outcomes generated by different allocations under fixed supply and show that it is governed by competition between vaccinating high-contact groups to slow transmission and vaccinating groups that benefit most directly: necessity is low when these protection routes are balanced and high when one dominates. Increasing transmission intensity changes this balance and drives a transition in the optimal allocation from transmission-focused prioritization toward direct protection. Different prevention objectives exhibit distinct transition thresholds, creating regimes in which optimizing one objective substantially compromises another, thereby revealing when the choice of prevention target matters most. This framework reframes vaccine prioritization as a prior decision problem, identifying when optimization is warranted, when simpler rules suffice, and when prevention goals conflict.

papers.title: Generalizable turbulence closures across bluff-body shapes by PINN-based solver-agnostic training
papers.summary: Data-driven turbulence closures are commonly calibrated by embedding a CFD solver within an inverse procedure that requires a converged flow solution at every optimization iteration, which is fragile and costly. We instead formulate closure identification as a PDE-constrained, data-driven inverse problem within a physics-informed neural network (PINN), and subsequently stabilize the inferred closure for deployment in a numerical solver. This separation eliminates the training cost of repeated CFD solves and associated adjoint or ensemble evaluations, providing substantial flexibility to investigate alternative closure forms. Using this flexibility, we develop four closures: three model the Reynolds stress on a realizable tensor basis---a local map, a non-local model transporting the turbulent kinetic energy and recovering the out-of-plane normal stress, and the same with a learned length scale $\ell$---and a fourth models the Reynolds force $\mathbf{F}=-\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol{\tau}$ directly, free of the realizability constraint. All four are trained across six two-dimensional bluff-body wakes at $Re=10^4$ and deployed frozen in a standard finite-element solver, stabilized primarily by input-gradient smoothing. Under a strict leave-one-shape-out (LOSO) protocol, all four reduce the field errors of a steady SST $k$-$\omega$ baseline, most strongly on the mean velocity. The learned-length-scale closure is most accurate on the stress fields, while the force model generalizes best on the mean velocity and drag (LOSO drag error $\sim 7\%$). The closures also train efficiently on Particle Image Velocimetry data, enabling geometries intractable for DNS.

papers.title: Photon-conserving Raman soliton attractors in focusing and defocusing Kerr media
papers.summary: The sign of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient has long been regarded as irrelevant to the direction of the Raman-induced soliton self-frequency shift. Yet the standard generalized nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (GNLSE) predicts a frequency shift that depends on the sign of the nonlinearity, which leads to an unphysical blue shift in the defocusing case. We resolve this inconsistency by deriving the time-domain form of the photon-conserving GNLSE (pcGNLSE) from its established frequency-domain counterpart. The derivation reveals that photon-number conservation imposes two sign modifications relative to the standard GNLSE: the Raman-shift coefficient acquires the absolute value of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient in place of its signed counterpart, and the self-steepening-Raman dissipation term likewise carries an absolute-value prefactor rather than a signed one. These two modifications jointly guarantee a universal spectral redshift and monotonically decreasing pulse energy during propagation, irrespective of the signs of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient and its frequency derivative. Applying the method of moments to the time-domain pcGNLSE with appropriate chirped ans\"atze, we derive closed-form evolution equations for five pulse parameters and establish explicit attractor conditions under which bright or dark Raman solitons propagate with constant peak power. Direct numerical integration of the pcGNLSE confirms all analytical predictions and demonstrates that the standard GNLSE fails qualitatively, predicting unphysical energy growth and spectral blueshift in the negative-nonlinearity regime. The results provide a rigorous analytical framework for Raman soliton dynamics in materials with negative third-order susceptibility, with direct implications for soliton-based devices in emerging semiconductor waveguide and microresonator platforms.

papers.title: Analysis of collisional and facility effects in a magnetic nozzle plasma expansion
papers.summary: An axisymmetric, quasineutral three-fluid model is proposed to study the plasma expansion in a magnetic nozzle under the presence of neutrals coming either from the plasma source or as an homogeneous background. As a difference with other models, electron cooling in the plume is achieved by treating the electron energy flux as mainly convective and without the need to postulate any anomalous resistivity. Solutions are presented for the electron high-magnetization limit, in which the electron main magnitudes can be integrated along magnetic lines. Ionization, elastic and charge-exchange collisions with neutrals do not change the main qualitative features of the plasma expansion, known from previous collisionless models. Ionization enhances the plasma flow in the nozzle, and leads to additional electron cooling, which decreases the electric potential fall along the nozzle. The efficiency of the nozzle is quantified in terms of the gain of magnetic thrust and the plume divergence angle. Two types of boundary conditions are discussed for the electron flow: local current ambipolarity conditions at the nozzle throat and global current-free conditions at the outer boundary (i.e., metallic vacuum chamber walls). These last ones are shown to be physically more reliable: they introduce the influence of the chamber walls on the plasma expansion by shaping the ambipolar electric field; they permit the extrapolation to undisturbed free space conditions; and they approximate better experimental trends with the background pressure.

papers.title: Strain-coupled one-dimensional turbulence: a single-line closure, its limits, and the consequence for leading-edge noise
papers.summary: Turbulence approaching a solid surface is strained before it arrives, and the distortion of its spectrum is often what governs the downstream response; yet reduced-order predictions, leading-edge-noise theory among them, still take the incoming spectrum as frozen. We develop a strain-coupled formulation of one-dimensional turbulence (ODT) that evolves strained turbulence with full spatial resolution at a cost compatible with parametric study, carrying the rapid distortion and the nonlinear relaxation together. The obstacle is that the rapid pressure-strain is non-local and three-dimensional while an ODT line resolves only the flow state along its own coordinate. Splitting the distortion physics by structure captures the phenomenology: the off-axis production and a spectrally closed rapid operator enter as continuous-in-time forcing along the model coordinate, while `eddy events' capture the on-line production and the turbulence-driven relaxation. Carried through to leading-edge noise, the evolved inflow shifts the predicted level by 5-20 dB at the energy-containing scales relative to the conventional frozen-spectrum assumption.

papers.title: AlgoPlasma: Open Algorithms for Plasma Modeling
papers.summary: AlgoPlasma is an open-source library in which core numerical algorithms for plasma modeling are implemented as modular, well-documented, and independently testable components. Rather than offering a complete simulation code, it allows researchers to select, adapt, and assemble the required components into application-specific workflows. The current release is centered on particle-based simulation, while AlgoPlasma is designed to encompass a broader range of approaches to plasma modeling. It provides components for particle initialization and advancement, particle-grid coupling, field solution, collision modeling, neutral transport, selected continuity updates, probe signal analysis, and input/output, together with Message Passing Interface (MPI) exchange routines and selected Open Multi-Processing (OpenMP) kernels. Documentation links mathematical formulations to source implementations, interfaces, and usage, while verification and validation cases evaluate numerical accuracy and physical behavior. AlgoPlasma thus establishes a shared algorithmic foundation for plasma modeling, transforming repeatedly reimplemented numerical methods into open, reusable, tested, and explainable components for research, verification, education, and collaborative development.

papers.title: Angle-domain null subtraction imaging from beamformed plane-wave data
papers.summary: Null subtraction imaging (NSI) narrows the apparent lateral response by combining fields produced with a zero-mean apodization and two DC-offset variants. Usually, NSI requires channel data and flexible beamformers (Receive-NSI). We investigate Angle-NSI, which operates on per-angle images during coherent plane-wave compounding. A matrix formulation was used to distinguish receive-domain and angle-domain null subtraction expressions. The method was evaluated using a simulated point target, experimental resolution phantom targets, an open microbubble (MB) traces dataset and two in vivo carotid acquisitions. Angle sampling, noise, phase jitter and target position were swept in simulation. A synchronized GPU benchmark compared the complete reconstructions. Six beamforming methods were compared: delay-and-sum (DAS), coherence-factor-weighted DAS (CF-DAS), minimum variance beamforming (MV), delay-multiply-and-sum (DMAS), Receive-NSI and Angle-NSI. Angle-NSI reduced the simulated -6 dB lateral width from 0.226 mm for DAS to 0.116 mm, compared with 0.009 mm for Receive-NSI, while the axial width was 0.720 mm for these three methods. The lateral narrowing was confirmed on an experimental resolution phantom. Angle-NSI had shorter reconstruction time than Receive-NSI and the lowest post-delay processing time among the nonlinear methods. In power Doppler, microbubble trace widths were reduced by 50.2% for Receive-NSI and 30.9% for Angle-NSI compared to DAS. On a phantom and in vivo, both NSI variants reduced generalized contrast-to-noise ratio relative to the conventional methods. Angle-NSI provides simple post-processing of per-angle beamformed images. It narrows the apparent lateral response at low computational cost, at the expense of B-mode detectability: this makes it a well-suited alternative for high-resolution power Doppler applications.

papers.title: Gas release from metals under irradiation with elliptic Gaussian laser beam during LID-QMS analysis
papers.summary: Laser-induced-desorption quadrupole-mass-spectrometry (LID-QMS) diagnostics is considered as one of the candidate methods for the remote control of tritium inventory in the ITER first wall. Studies involving LID-QMS generally assume the circular shape of the laser spot on the analyzed surface. At the same time, the diagnostics laser source cannot be always positioned so as to irradiate tokamak tiles under normal angles, which results in the laser spot shape differing from the circular one. In this contribution, we analyze the tritium removal process under sample irradiation by an elliptic Gaussian laser beam, extending the results of our previous analysis [A.A. Stepanenko, Yu.M. Gasparyan, Physica Scripta 99 (8), 085604 (2025)]. The thermal desorption model governing the heat transport and tritium removal from the solid is formulated. The new analytical expression describing the sample temperature dynamics is derived. The developed model is used to examine the impact of the laser beam/spot ellipticity on the tritium desorption process from a tungsten sample. The conditions, under which the elliptic beam can be approximated with the circular one for the rapid assessment of the amount of desorbed tritium, are assessed.

papers.title: Braided endovascular implants for intracranial aneurysms: mechanics, hemodynamics, and clinical translation
papers.summary: Endovascular implants prevent intracranial aneurysm rupture by altering the mechanical and hemodynamic environment at the aneurysm neck. Yet many in silico workflows prescribe or reconstruct the post-deployment geometry before computing flow, leaving unresolved the mechanics that create the clinically relevant interface. Here we review braided intraluminal flow diverters, intrasaccular devices, and emerging flow-disruption concepts across deployment mechanics, inter-wire and wire-wall contact, superelasticity, wall apposition, pore geometry, computational fluid dynamics, and fluid-structure interaction. We connect these modeling choices to neck coverage, malapposition, migration, deformation, and durability, and distinguish established evidence from mechanistic inference and prospective hypotheses. We argue that model fidelity should match the clinical question: prescribed or fast placement may support screening, whereas questions of coverage, apposition, compaction, and migration benefit from mechanically plausible deployment states. An interface-resolved mechanics-to-flow framework, supported by measurable validation targets and standardized reporting, could improve device design and enable more reliable patient-specific treatment planning.

papers.title: $f$-2$f$ self-referencing for silicon nitride photonics via a heterogeneously integrated lithium niobate layer
papers.summary: Heterogeneous integration combines complementary material properties in a single photonic platform. Here, we demonstrate on-chip $f$-2$f$ self-referencing in a heterogeneously integrated Si$_3$N$_4$/LiNbO$_3$ platform, in which supercontinuum generation in a Si$_3$N$_4$ waveguide and second-harmonic generation in a LiNbO$_3$ layer are spatially separated and linked by adiabatic escalator couplers. Pumped by a 1560 nm mode-locked laser with 75 pJ on-chip pulse energy, we detect the carrier-envelope offset frequency with 30 dB signal-to-noise ratio in 300 kHz resolution bandwidth. A comparative measurement confirms that the second harmonic originates in the LiNbO$_3$ layer and indicates opportunity for further improvements through periodic poling. These results establish heterogeneous Si$_3$N$_4$/LiNbO$_3$ integration as a viable building block for self-referenced ultrafast pulse sources in low-loss Si$_3$N$_4$ photonics.

papers.title: Thermocapillary stabilization of Liquid Space Telescopes
papers.summary: We investigate how spatially uniform, time-modulated heating can be used to stabilize a thin liquid mirror in microgravity. Periodic heating generates oscillatory thermocapillary flows that suppress the instability associated with sustained heating, allowing the free surface to relax through the combined effects of thermal radiation, thermocapillary transport, and capillarity. Using multiple-scale analysis of a long-wave model, we derive the coupled surface-temperature evolution over many heating cycles. A subsequent linear stability analysis yields the stability criteria and decay times of individual surface modes. Numerical simulations validate the analytical predictions and demonstrate stabilization of meter-scale surface deformations over timescales of days.

papers.title: Chiroptical Nonlinearity Found in Covalent Organic Frameworks
papers.summary: Chiroptical nonlinearity is vital for modern optics and photonics. However, it remains a central challenge to obtain a material simultaneously with large second-order nonlinearity and strong nonlinear optical chirality. Here we uncover the strong chiroptical nonlinearity in COF-330-a, owing to the formation of unique chiral, polar structure with large p-electron conjugation via structural transformation. A large effective second-order nonlinear susceptibility of ~ 101 pm/V and a strong nonlinear chiroptical response (SHG-CD: -1.60 to +1.66) have been demonstrated in individual COF-330-a microcrystals, transcending the performance trade-off limitation in conventional chiroptical materials. These findings open a new avenue for designing nonlinear chiroptical materials which harness the duality of polarity and chirality and chemical versatility of COFs.

papers.title: LAO+: Focused, Multi-Replica Accelerated Orthogonal Sampling for Robust Binding Free Energy Predictions
papers.summary: We introduce Lambda-ABF-OPES+ ($\text{LAO+}$), a multi-replica framework for absolute binding free energy (ABFE) calculations that accelerates both the alchemical transformation and the slow ``orthogonal'' motions coupled to it. At the core of $\text{LAO+}$ is a partitioned $\lambda$-dynamics scheme that concentrates sampling on the abrupt rehydration of the binding pocket, the main bottleneck of ligand decoupling, while Hamiltonian replica exchange relays configurations along the entire alchemical path. This drives a fourfold gain in convergence speed for the rate-limiting leg over our previous $\text{LAO}$ method, which was itself up to ninefold faster than Lambda-ABF, an overall gain of up to $\sim$36-fold. Applied to 28 protein--ligand complexes across five targets, $\text{LAO+}$ achieves a root-mean-square error of 0.83~kcal~mol$^{-1}$ and a correlation of 0.87 with experiment from only 63~ns of sampling per ligand. Moreover, dedicated reservoir replicas accelerate any slow degree of freedom that can be described by a collective variable. We demonstrate this by recovering hidden protein and ligand conformational states, for example in T4 lysozyme, BRD4 and JNK1. Together, these advances make accurate ABFE calculations practical for drug discovery.

papers.title: Integrated Open-Source Framework for Simulation of Transcatheter Pulmonary Valves in Native Right Ventricular Outflow Tracts
papers.summary: Pulmonary insufficiency is a consequence of transannular patch repair in Tetralogy of Fallot (ToF), leading to late morbidity and mortality. Transcatheter native outflow tract pulmonary valve replacement (TPVR) has become common, but assessment of patient candidacy and selection of the optimal device remains challenging. We demonstrate an integrated open-source workflow for simulation of TPVR in image-derived models to inform device selection. Machine learning-based segmentation of Computer Tomography (CT) scans was implemented to define the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT). A custom workflow for device positioning and pre-compression was implemented in SlicerHeart. Resulting geometries were exported to FEBio for simulation. Visualization of results and quantification were performed using custom metrics implemented in SlicerHeart and FEBio. RVOT model creation and device placement could be completed in under 1 minute. Virtual device placement using FE simulations visually mimicked actual device placement and allowed quantification of vessel strain, stress, and contact area. Regions of higher strain and stress were observed at the proximal and distal end locations of the TPVs where the devices impinge on the RVOT wall. No other consistent trends were observed across simulations. The observed variability in mechanical metrics across RVOTS, stents, and locations in the RVOT highlights that no single device performs optimally in all anatomies, thereby reinforcing the need for simulation-based patient-specific assessment. This study demonstrates the feasibility of a novel open-source workflow for the rapid simulation of TPVR, which, with further refinement, may inform assessment of patient candidacy and optimal device selection.

papers.title: Grain Boundary Anisotropy and Its Influence on Helium Bubble Nucleation, Growth, and Decohesion in Polycrystalline Iron
papers.summary: The accumulation of helium bubbles at grain boundaries (GBs) critically degrades the mechanical integrity of structural materials in nuclear reactors. While GBs act as sinks for radiation-induced defects, their inherent structural anisotropy leads to complex helium bubble evolution behaviors that remain poorly understood. This work integrates accelerated molecular dynamics simulations and a novel atomic-scale metric, the flexibility volume (V_f), to establish the interplay between GB character, helium segregation, and bubble growth mechanisms in body-centered cubic iron. We demonstrate that V_f, which incorporates both local atomic volume and vibrational properties, qualitatively predicts deformation propensity. Our results reveal that the atomic-scale segregation energy landscape dictates initial helium clustering and subsequent bubble morphology, with low-energy channels in tilt {\Sigma}5 boundary facilitating one-dimensional migration while isolated deep traps in twist {\Sigma}13 boundary promote larger, rounder bubble morphology. Critically, besides gradual bubble growth via trap mutation mechanism, we identify two distinct stress-relief mechanisms: loop punching in anisotropic tilt {\Sigma}5 boundary and interfacial decohesion in twist {\Sigma}11 boundary, with the dominant pathway determined by the interplay between bubble morphology and local mechanical softness. This study establishes a fundamental connection between GB crystallographic and energetical anisotropy and helium bubble evolution, providing critical insights for designing radiation-tolerant microstructures.

papers.title: Empirical Quantum Advantage in Constrained Optimization from Encoded Unitary Designs
papers.summary: We introduce the Constraint-Enhanced Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (CE-QAOA), a shallow, constraint-aware ansatz that operates inside the one-hot product space [n]^m, where m is the number of blocks and each block is initialized in an n-qubit W_n state. We give an ancilla-free, depth-optimal encoder that prepares W_n using n-1 two-qubit rotations per block, and a two-local block-XY mixer that preserves the one-hot manifold and has a constant spectral gap on the one-excitation sector. At the level of expressivity, we establish per-block controllability, implying approximate universality per block. At the level of distributional behavior, we show that, after natural block and symbol permutation twirls, shallow CE-QAOA realizes an encoded unitary 1-design and supports approximate second-moment (2-design) behavior; combined with a Paley-Zygmund argument, this yields finite-shot anticoncentration guarantees. Algorithmically, we wrap constant-depth sampling with a deterministic feasibility checker to obtain a polynomial-time hybrid quantum-classical solver (PHQC) that returns the best observed feasible solution in O(S n^2) time, where S is a polynomial shot budget. We obtain two advantages. First, when CE-QAOA fixes r >= 1 locations different from the start city, we achieve a Theta(n^r) reduction in shot complexity even against a classical sampler that draws uniformly from the feasible set. Second, against a classical baseline restricted to raw bitstring sampling, we show an exp(Theta(n^2)) minimax separation. In noiseless circuit simulations of traveling salesman problem instances with n in {4,...,10} locations from the QOPTLib benchmark library, we recover the global optimum at depth p = 1 using polynomial shot budgets and coarse parameter grids defined by the problem size.

papers.title: Simulation of topological superconductors and their competing orders using photon-mediated interactions
papers.summary: Realizing and controlling the unconventional pairing featured by topological superconductors remains a central challenge. We introduce a cavity QED quantum simulator that engineers competing chiral $p_x+ip_y$ and $d_{x^2-y^2}+id_{xy}$ orders by tailoring cavity-mediated couplings between atomic pseudospins that emulate momentum-dependent pairing channels. The desired spatially inhomogeneous cavity-mediated couplings can be engineered in a 2D optical lattice using incommensurate cavity-lattice wavelengths naturally occurring in cavity QED systems. This minimal and fully tunable platform enables controlled state preparation and continuous measurement of superconducting order parameters. To probe this competition, the platform enables selective excitation and direct time-domain detection of Bardasis-Schrieffer modes---collective excitations of the subdominant pairing channel. The same competing channel can have an even stronger impact out of equilibrium, where a sudden quench can drive its growth and abruptly reshape the dominant superconducting order, despite the stability of the dominant order in equilibrium. Together, these results establish cavity QED as a controlled setting for revealing hidden competing orders and exploring nonlinear dynamics of topological superconductivity that remain elusive in solid-state and ultracold-atom systems.

papers.title: Realization of a cavity-coupled Rydberg array
papers.summary: Scalable quantum computers and quantum networks require the combination of quantum processing nodes with efficient light-matter interfaces to distribute quantum information in local or long-distance quantum networks. Neutral-atom arrays have both been coupled to Rydberg states to enable high-fidelity quantum gates in universal processing architectures, and to optical cavities to realize interfaces to photons. However, combining these two capabilities and coupling atom arrays to highly excited Rydberg states in the mode of an optical cavity has been an outstanding challenge. Here we present a novel cavity-coupled Rydberg array that achieves this long-standing goal. We prepare, detect, and control individual atoms in a scalable optical tweezer array, couple them strongly to the optical mode of a high-finesse optical cavity and excite them in a controlled way to Rydberg states. We show that high-cooperativity coupling to an optical cavity -- demonstrated via the dispersive shift of the resonance of the cavity in presence of the atoms -- and strong Rydberg interactions -- demonstrated via the collective enhancement of Rydberg coupling in the atomic array -- can be achieved in our setup at the same spatial location. Our presented experimental platform opens the path to several new directions, including the realization of quantum network nodes, quantum simulation of long-range interacting, open quantum systems and photonic-state engineering leveraging high-fidelity Rydberg control.

papers.title: Time-Rescaled STIRAP Enables Compact Cascaded Frequency Conversion
papers.summary: In this letter we explore how full frequency conversion can be performed in shorter optical devices by using a STIRAP-like protocol modified by the time rescaling shortcut to adiabaticity. We first show a detailed, step-by-step process of how the coupled equations for two simultaneous three-wave mixing processes can be written in terms of a STIRAP-like system. From the properties of the STIRAP protocol, we know that the ensuing process will result in robust conversion, but require long propagation distances inside the bulk crystal or waveguide. We then apply the time rescaling shortcut to adiabaticty in the conversion process to create a TR-STIRAP protocol, showing that full and robust conversion is also obtained, but at a fraction of the propagation distance. We also show how the original shaping of the coupling coefficients required by the TR-STIRAP can be approximated by Gaussian functions with high conversion fidelity, thus simplifying the experimental implementation. Finally, a possible application of the new protocol is discussed in the context of single-photon detection in the MIR.

papers.title: Simulating cavity QED with spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates revisited
papers.summary: Simulating cavity quantum electrodynamics in synthetic platforms offers a route to studying light--matter physics without real photons. We reassess the frequently invoked analogy between harmonically trapped, spin--orbit-coupled atoms and the quantum Rabi and Dicke models, with particular emphasis on squeezing and entanglement. A single non-interacting atom realizes the quantum Rabi Hamiltonian exactly, up to elementary spin and phase-space rotations. For $N$ non-interacting atoms, however, the center-of-mass mode is only one member of a complete orthonormal set containing $N-1$ relative modes. We prove that, after all modes are included, the spin--spin terms generated by the collective mode cancel exactly against those generated by the relative modes. Equivalently, the original Hamiltonian is a sum of independent one-particle Hamiltonians and therefore cannot create interparticle entanglement from a separable state. Contact interactions invalidate this cancellation but do not remove the relative modes or turn the exact many-body Hamiltonian into a Dicke model. A one-mode Dicke description can arise only as a controlled low-energy approximation after all relevant relative excitations have been shown to be spectrally suppressed. We discuss this distinction together with experimental scales, finite temperature, and possible mode-selection strategies. We also distinguish the single-particle interference underlying density fringes from the interaction-stabilized stripe supersolid observed in many-body condensates.

papers.title: Various phases of active matter emerging from bacteria and their implications
papers.summary: In this perspective article, we discuss bacterial populations as a model system of active matter. It allows for the exploration and characterization of various phases of active matter and brings rich implications for both physics and biology. Specifically, we focus on active gas, active liquid, active glass and active liquid crystal states observed in bacterial populations and describe how these differ from their thermal counterparts. A few future directions are also discussed that will deepen the physical interest in active matter as a new type of material, with its implications for several life phenomena observed in bacterial populations and other biological systems.

papers.title: Partially reactive force field for the UiO-66 metal-organic framework
papers.summary: UiO-66 is the most widely studied metal-organic framework, on account of its structural tunability given by its capacity of sustaining high amounts of point defects in its structure. Its synthesis mechanism is largely unknown, with only a few works mostly focused on the formation of the Zr-oxide cluster. In this work, a partially reactive force field to model UiO-66, nb-UiO-FF, is introduced. This force field incorporates node--ligand reactivity via a Morse potential and the introduction of dummy atoms to reproduce the anisotropic charge distribution of the Zr atoms in the node. nb-UiO-FF reproduces structural features of both UiO-66 and its isoreticular analog UiO-67 as well as framework stability with or without defects, activated or filled with N,N-dimethylformamide or ethanol. Defect generation and node--ligand binding energies are comparable with density functional theory values. The force field is further employed within a molecular dynamics scheme to study the early stages of solvothermal node--ligand binding. Species with structures corresponding to motifs present in UiO-66 are observed, along with other metastable species. This force field enables studying the self-assembly of UiO-66, as well as the formation of its point defects.

papers.title: Absorption and Phase-Contrast Microtomography Using Direct X-Ray Detection With Commercial Off-The-Shelf CMOS Sensors
papers.summary: This work presents high-resolution X-ray microtomography based on commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) CMOS image sensors as direct detectors. The system uses a microfocus X-ray source in cone-beam geometry, enabling both absorption-contrast imaging, thanks to the sensor s intrinsic resolution, and phase-contrast imaging, by adjusting the object-to-sensor distance. A dynamic flat-field correction algorithm mitigates radiation-induced sensor degradation during long acquisitions. The setup provides voxel sizes from 3.9 microns to 5.2 microns, with an effective spatial resolution (FWHM) as fine as 9.6 microns in magnified phase-contrast mode (1.33x) and 21 microns in non-magnified absorption-contrast mode. Phase contrast enhances visualization of soft tissue boundaries that are difficult to visualize using absorption-contrast imaging in the same experimental configuration.

papers.title: Dynamic models with $p$ parameters are identified by $2p+1$ random features
papers.summary: A foundational principle in nonlinear dynamics is that the structure of a dynamical system can be recovered from a small number of generic measurements or coordinates. We develop an analogous principle for the identification of dynamic models for time series \textit{with noise}, which builds on previous identification results for noiseless dynamical systems. The noise is allowed to be non-iid, non-Gaussian, and dependent on the state. Our results cover noisily observed differential equations and discrete-time dynamical systems, as well as stochastic models with process noise. We illustrate the utility of this identification principle using a Lorenz-63 model and a H\'{e}non map model, both with observational noise.

papers.title: Estimating dynamic models by matching random features
papers.summary: Scientists increasingly express their ideas as dynamic models of complex processes. It is often much easier to simulate these models than to calculate the probability of their generating a particular outcome, making likelihood-based estimation infeasible. Existing likelihood-free approaches rely either on manually chosen summary statistics or on representations learned by neural networks. The former is error-prone and laborious, while the latter is computationally intensive, leaving many scientists in a difficult position. We show that, for a large class of dynamic models, parameters can be estimated by matching a small number of random features of the observed and simulated data. In particular, we show that models with a $p$-dimensional parameter can be identified from just $2p+1$ generic random Fourier features. We introduce two estimators for stationary and nonstationary processes, respectively, and we establish their consistency under mild regularity conditions. More broadly, our results serve as the foundation for a new class of methods for simulation-based inference.

papers.title: Controlling Turbulent Flows in Compressible Active Liquid Crystals
papers.summary: Motivated by experiments on light-patterned, quasi-2D active suspensions that exhibit large density variations, we develop a continuum theory of compressible active nematics--suspensions of apolar rods whose orientation is invariant under $\pi$ rotations. Under spatially patterned activity, the extensile isotropic active pressure expels material from high-activity regions and accumulates it in low-activity ones; an exactly solvable scalar reduction shows that the resulting density contrast is governed by a single dimensionless parameter, linear in the compressibility. Using compressibility as a tuning knob, we then steer active turbulence from high- to low-activity regions and, at sharp activity interfaces, stabilize an analytically tractable dynamical steady state: a one-dimensional chain of vortices held by soft, activity-induced confinement. Our results establish compressibility as a control parameter for density variations and turbulent flow in active nematic suspensions.

papers.title: Picometre-scale real-time drift correction in TEM and STEM by dynamic control of the specimen stage for atomic-resolution imaging
papers.summary: In this work, we show how the specimen drift can be actively compensated by controlling the stage with precision down to the picometre scale. We do this by dynamic control, a generic real-time feedback framework designed to actively stabilize electron microscopy experiments by continuously monitoring an experimental variable from the detector data stream and compensating its evolution during acquisition. The framework, applicable to a broad range of controllable experimental instabilities, includes automated calibration procedures, operates in parallel with image acquisition and is implemented as a software plugin without requiring any hardware modification of the microscope. Results for live drift correction are shown for a selection of TEM and STEM instruments using conventional mechanical stages as well as piezoelectric stages. Experimental results are presented for medium resolution TEM, high-resolution TEM, HR-STEM and in situ observations. With piezoelectric stages, specimen stabilization down to the picometre scale was achieved allowing drift-corrected atomic-resolution imaging. Specimen stage-based stabilization significantly improves long-exposure imaging and in situ experiments by increasing the effective exposure time, preserving the field of view, maintaining identical optical conditions and eliminating the need for numerical alignment of large datasets. Beyond the specific application presented here, dynamic control provides a versatile framework for real-time regulation of electron microscopy experiments and opens new perspectives for quantitative imaging, automated in situ studies and multimodal acquisitions.

papers.title: Electronic Properties of Ladder-Type Phenylenes Studied by Thermally-Assisted-Occupation Density Functional Theory
papers.summary: Accurate prediction of the electronic properties of extended $\pi$-conjugated systems with radical character remains a major theoretical challenge. To overcome this challenge, thermally-assisted-occupation density functional theory (TAO-DFT) has been developed in recent years. In this study, we employ TAO-DFT to systematically explore the electronic properties of ladder-type phenylenes ($n$-LPs), containing $n$ linearly fused four-membered carbon rings. Our calculations reveal that all investigated $n$-LPs (with $n$ = 1 ~ 40) possess singlet ground states. With increasing $n$-LP length, we observe a transition from the nonradical character of shorter $n$-LPs to the polyradical character of longer $n$-LPs. Notably, we identify a distinct damped periodic oscillation in the radical character of $n$-LPs, featuring highly correlated hotspots at specific lengths ($n = 3k - 1$, where $k$ are positive integers). The real-space representation of active orbitals confirms this global electronic behavior is governed by the intrinsic structural periodicity and completely delocalized nature of the active orbitals along the central ladder framework. These findings provide fundamental insights into the size-dependent electronic properties of $n$-LPs, guiding their rational design for future nanomaterial applications.

papers.title: Domain of Applicability of the Distorted Wave Born Approximation (DWBA): A Critical Analysis for X-ray and Visible-Light Interface Scattering
papers.summary: The Distorted Wave Born Approximation (DWBA) is established for X-ray interface scattering, yet its domain of applicability has never been stated explicitly. The DWBA implicitly rests on the small refractive index deviation (SRID) condition - satisfied by X-rays ($|n-1| \sim 10^{-6}$) but violated by visible light ($|n-1| \sim 0.5$). The DWBA mixes microscopic and macroscopic Maxwell equations, whereas a rigorous optical theory must be built on the macroscopic Maxwell equations and constitutive relations. Rigorous alternatives for two specific inconsistencies in the standard DWBA are discussed. The Extended Transfer Matrix Approach (ETMA) for visible-light interface scattering is outlined.

papers.title: Worldsheet string theory on $\mathrm{AdS}_3 \times \mathbf{S}^3 \times \mathrm{K3}$
papers.summary: The RNS formalism describing string theory on $\mathrm{AdS}_3 \times \mathbf{S}^3 \times \mathrm{K3}$ supported by pure NS-NS flux is in principle straightforward to write down. One can directly check that the worldsheet theory reproduces the correct chiral spectrum expected from supergravity by analyzing the BRST cohomology. However, when one attempts to construct the worldsheet partition function using the standard rules of the RNS formalism by appropriately summing over spin structures to ensure worldsheet modular invariance, one finds a result in tension with spacetime supersymmetry. We explain why this is the case and, more importantly, propose a resolution. Specifically, we fix the physical state projection for the partition function uniquely by requiring spacetime supersymmetry. Perhaps surprisingly, the projected worldsheet partition function does not factorize into a bosonic and a fermionic part and involves functions that are not modular covariant. As a consistency check, we show that our prescription for the worldsheet partition function reproduces the supergravity spectrum for both Type IIB and IIA theories. Furthermore, we compute the elliptic genus of the dual CFT from the worldsheet, which has both a holomorphic short string and a non-holomorphic long string contribution. The latter displays characteristics of a mock modular function, albeit with some key differences, while the former has the tantalizing structure of a symmetric orbifold. We also point out the worldsheet construction of a non-supersymmetric theory, whose spectrum is free of tachyons.

papers.title: An SYK wormhole under the microscope
papers.summary: We derive a large-N wormhole saddle in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model for the variance of the thermal one-point function of a heavy operator across realizations of the microscopic couplings. We propose that this saddle describes a double trumpet geometry. In the double-scaling limit, we express the wormhole as a transition amplitude in an emergent bulk Hilbert space of chords connecting the two boundaries. In the Schwarzian limit, the chords proliferate and the wormhole defines a quantum transition amplitude in the open-universe Hilbert space of Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity. Comparing the SYK wormhole amplitude with its counterpart in JT gravity coupled to matter provides a direct test of the heavy-operator randomness hypothesis in SYK. The microscopic SYK couplings specify the {\alpha}-parameters of the wormhole. For a fixed realization of the couplings, we compute the observable in the corresponding {\alpha}-state. We provide the bulk wavefunction of the associated half-wormhole, which exhibits erratic correlations in the length basis that do not self-average. We extend the bulk description to the Hilbert space of a closed universe. We point out that the correlation chords from which the wormhole geometry emerges structurally resemble local observer worldlines.

papers.title: Region bounds, error margins and certified positivity in the numerical conformal bootstrap; Or the first mathematically rigorous bounds on the 3d Ising CFT critical exponents
papers.summary: Numerical conformal bootstrap bounds are commonly called rigorous, yet as published they are not theorems: they hold at sampled points rather than on regions of parameter space, for truncated rational approximations of the conformal blocks, for a finite list of spins, and up to floating-point rounding. We close all four gaps. We show how to search efficiently for functionals positive on regions, including external-dimension space; how positivity on the large-spin crossing vectors can be imposed as such a region constraint; how new analytic bounds on the conformal-block recursion relations give functionals positive on the true, untruncated crossing vectors; and how to certify the positivity of these functionals in exact arithmetic. The certification rests on Bernstein-basis positivity certificates in up to three variables, exact arithmetic in $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)$, a compactified treatment of the infinite spin tail, and an explicit bound on the difference between the true blocks and their truncations, so that infinitely many positivity conditions reduce to finitely many machine-checked sign conditions. As a flagship application we certify an exclusion region in the $(\Delta_\sigma,\Delta_\epsilon)$ plane: for $\Delta_\sigma\in[0.505,0.5405]$ all of $\Delta_\epsilon\in(1/2,3]$ is excluded except a small rectangle containing the 3d Ising island, giving rigorous two-sided bounds on the critical exponents $\eta$ and $\nu$ under explicitly stated spectrum assumptions. The analytic inputs for the mixed $\sigma$-$\epsilon$ system, which would remove the spin-2 gap assumption, are also proved. The same methods prevent common practical failure modes and can make bootstrap searches faster: region bounds turn the mapping of an island into a handful of one-dimensional bisections. The essential code to reproduce the search and the certification, and all machine-checkable certificates, are released.

papers.title: Finite-cutoff geometry from double-scaled SYK
papers.summary: We develop a finite-cutoff holographic description of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We construct microscopic deformations of Kourkoulou-Maldacena and thermofield-double SYK states whose double-scaling limits reproduce a lower-dimensional analogue of $\text{T}\overline{\text{T}}$ and $\text{T}\overline{\text{T}}+\Lambda_2$ deformations, which we denote $T^2$ and $T^2+\Lambda_1$, respectively. The ensemble-averaged theory describes wormhole states in finite-cutoff sine dilaton gravity, and finite-cutoff anti-de Sitter and de Sitter geometries in the low- and high-energy regimes, respectively. The analysis includes both perturbative and non-perturbative solutions to the energy spectrum flow equation, and the regions behind and beyond the respective horizons. Only the perturbative branch admits physical quantum states. We study how to incorporate end-of-the-world (ETW) branes in the finite cutoff holographic dictionary. The ETW brane leads to an additional boundary theory deformation, which leads to black hole or eternal traversable wormhole geometries depending on the existence of normalizable bound states. We extend the finite cutoff length evaluations for constant mean curvature (CMC) slices, and interpret them as complexity in the boundary theory. We discuss possible extensions with matter. Our results provide a microscopic framework for studying the finite-cutoff boundaries, CMC slices and branes in the holographic dictionary of DSSYK.

papers.title: Gluon Scattering in Expanding de Sitter Universe
papers.summary: We construct an observer-centric S-matrix in the expanding Poincar\'e patch of four-dimensional de Sitter space. The asymptotic states are defined along the worldline of a comoving, or eternal, observer, the only kind of geodesic observer that remains in the patch for all proper time, and the free Hamiltonian is the conserved charge generating translations in her proper time. The resulting S-matrix is independent of which eternal observer is chosen. We apply the construction to pure Yang--Mills theory in Coulomb gauge and compute the three- and four-gluon amplitudes at tree level. The amplitudes have a structure similar to the cosmological correlators of gauge currents and are constrained by the Ward identities of de Sitter isometries.

papers.title: 6d SCFTs and terminal singularities
papers.summary: The classification of 6d $\mathcal{N}=(1,0)$ SCFTs has been carried out with great success, enumerating consistent elliptically fibered threefolds in F-theory. In this note, we observe that the E-string 6d SCFT can be decorated with extra matter sectors. This decoration exploits an opening allowed by the current classification, implementing terminal singularities nested on the curve of the base of the elliptic fibration that supplies the tensor branch. Additionally, via dimensional reduction on a circle, we identify versions of the 5d $E_n$ theories decorated by extra matter sectors. As a bonus, the end of the resulting RG flow cascade reproduces a 5d theory recently constructed in the literature, explaining its 6d origin. We remain agnostic as to whether the decorated 6d and 5d theories constitute novel SCFTs.

papers.title: Orientation-Dependent Casimir Energy and Generalized Torque in Lorentz-Violating Rectangular Compactifications
papers.summary: We derive the renormalized Casimir energy of a free massive real scalar field on the rectangular compactification \(\mathbb{R}^{1,r}\times T^p\) in the presence of a constant CPT-even aether-like Lorentz-violating background. Allowing the spatial part of the background vector to have an arbitrary orientation relative to the compactification lattice, we characterize the resulting orientation-dependent geometric response of the vacuum. Integrating out the noncompact momenta reduces the effective spatial kinetic matrix to its Schur complement, and Poisson resummation yields a closed, exponentially convergent Bessel-function lattice sum within the stability domain. The resulting expression separates an orientation-independent kinetic normalization, \([1+\lambda u_\mu u^\mu]^{-1/2}\), from an orientation-dependent deformation of the image-lattice metric. Coordinate-aligned configurations are recovered as special cases, and the exact massless limit and the compact-direction pressures are obtained. For a two-dimensional compact subspace, we explicitly analyze the angular dependence of the vacuum energy and derive the associated generalized Casimir torque. These results establish how the relative orientation between a Lorentz-violating background and an anisotropic compactification lattice enters the renormalized vacuum energy and its directional response.

papers.title: The Magic Barrier: A Universal Feature of Quantum Thermalization
papers.summary: We show that the emergence of a ``magic barrier'', characterized by a transient maximum of nonstabilizerness during rapid entanglement growth, is a universal feature of thermalization within quantum ergodic theories, which is intimately connected to random matrix spectral properties. Starting from a pure product state, we analytically determine the time evolution of entanglement entropy, antiflatness, capacity of entanglement, and nonlocal trace distance magic under unitary dynamics generated by random matrix Hamiltonians drawn from all three Gaussian ensembles. We find that the transient maxima of antiflatness, capacity of entanglement, and nonlocal magic occur on the same characteristic timescale as the maximum rate of entanglement growth. These results establish that the magic barrier is a universal feature of RMT thermalization, suggesting universality across quantum chaotic systems. We conclude that quantitative simulations of thermalization in ergodic quantum theories inherently require quantum computation.

papers.title: All Order Gravitational Wave Tails for Subleading Post-Newtonian Expansion
papers.summary: The low-frequency gravitational waveform emitted in a classical scattering process contains an infinite tower of late- and early-time tail terms of the form $u^{-r}(\ln|u|)^{r-1}$, $r \geq 1$. In the Newtonian limit, the coefficients of this entire tower have recently been shown to be universal, i.e. fixed by the asymptotic data of the scattering objects alone. At the retained order in the velocity expansion, these leading-logarithmic tails are determined to all orders in Newton's constant $G$. We extend this result to the first subleading order in the post-Newtonian expansion of the asymptotic states. We consider scattering of an arbitrary number of incoming and outgoing nonrelativistic objects interacting only through gravity at long range, and we derive the complete tower of tail terms at this order. The correction arises from the first subleading term in the retardation expansion and is determined by the asymptotic Newtonian trajectories of the massive particles. Its coefficients are again determined entirely by the asymptotic trajectories and are independent of the details of the interaction. For $2\to2$ scattering, the leading-logarithmic series can be summed in closed form. Our results agree with a relativistic conjecture proposed in earlier work arXiv:2610.07134.

papers.title: Exact AdS and pp-waves in multi-gravity beyond pairwise interactions
papers.summary: We construct exact anti-de Sitter (AdS) waves and pp-waves in ghost-free multi-gravity beyond pairwise interactions for an arbitrary number $\mathcal{N}$ of vielbeins, in any spacetime dimension $D\geq3$. Deforming proportional AdS and Minkowski solutions along a common null direction reduces the full nonlinear field equations to coupled linear differential equations for the wave profiles, without restricting their amplitudes. The system is diagonalised in the same eigenbasis as the perturbative Fierz-Pauli mass matrix, separating the solutions into one massless and $\mathcal{N}-1$ massive eigenprofiles. We obtain explicit radial and transverse solutions and impose an AdS boundary falloff. This falloff admits the appropriate radial branch of every mode with non-negative squared mass and excludes profiles with negative squared masses, including logarithmic solutions at the Breitenlohner-Freedman threshold. We also relate the AdS waves to pp-waves through a local flat limit. Explicit examples exhibit wave configurations that cannot be reproduced by ghost-free pairwise theories, demonstrating that genuine multi-field interactions support new exact gravitational-wave solutions.

papers.title: Beyond the polynomial ansatz: regular $AdS_3\times M_8$ solutions of M-theory
papers.summary: We study regular compact solutions of the cohomogeneity-one $AdS_3\times M_8$ system of Gauntlett, Mac Conamhna, Mateos and Waldram, where $M_8$ is an $S^2$ bundle over three constant-curvature Riemann surfaces. We find that an endpoint argument rules out every non-flat curvature-sign sector without a positive-curvature factor, while an analytic deformation gives regular families with four radial shape parameters in all remaining sectors, with the base geometry held fixed. The known polynomial solutions form a proper analytic locus in these families. Non-polynomiality is therefore generic in parameter space, although the deviation from an endpoint-matching polynomial can be very small. Apart from the completely flat exception, the curvature-sign criterion is necessary and sufficient within this ansatz. Four magnetic flux ratios give local coordinates near the reference solution and its small-curvature deformations, and a rational inverse reconstructs candidate endpoint data directly from finite flux ratios. In the fully positive sector we prove that one explicit four-dimensional finite-ratio neighbourhood lies inside the physical flux image. The magnetic periods and leading holographic central charge reduce to endpoint data, and, once the common Brown--Henneaux normalization is fixed, the nontrivial flux dependence of the equivariant localization formula agrees with the endpoint result as an exact algebraic identity. We also quantify the non-polynomial corrections and analyse finite degenerations under explicit convergence hypotheses.

papers.title: Stability and dynamics of bumblebee models
papers.summary: In this work, we study vector field theories with spontaneous Lorentz violation induced by a nonderivative potential $V(X)$ (with $X = B_\mu B^\mu$), known as bumblebee models, with a Maxwell kinetic term in Minkowski spacetime. We confirm a recent result showing that a class of smooth potentials, including a purely cubic potential, leads to a Hamiltonian density that is bounded from below and assumes a global minimum for nonzero timelike expectation values of the vector field satisfying $X = b^2 > 0$, inducing spontaneous Lorentz-symmetry breaking. We show explicitly that the standard quadratic potential has a Hamiltonian that is unbounded from below and thus unstable. We analyze the Hamiltonian equations of motion for the timelike case and demonstrate that they are regular at the global minimum. Furthermore, we examine the linearized spectrum of small fluctuations around the minimum. We also study particular solutions with spherical symmetry analytically and numerically, without assuming linearization. We find that the time evolution of smooth initial configurations can develop shock-like singularities, and we explain why this behavior is expected in this model. We also identify a subset of the space of field configurations in which the field equations cease to be hyperbolic, leading to a breakdown of well-posedness of the Cauchy initial-value problem.
