papers.title: Exciton superfluidity in two-dimensional bilayers at zero and high magnetic fields
papers.summary: We study interlayer exciton superfluidity versus layer separation in two-dimensional electron-hole bilayers at zero magnetic field and quantum Hall bilayers at total filling $\nu_T=1$. Unscreened Hartree-Fock theory predicts coherence at every finite separation, with an energy scale decaying inversely with separation at large distances. We examine how screening, correlations, and spatial instabilities modify this prediction. At zero field, we solve the linearized gap equation with the full momentum and frequency dependence of the interaction screened within the random-phase approximation, without an imposed cutoff. The apparent plasmon enhancement of pairing in the ladder approximation is largely cancelled by the second-order crossed-rung correction. Static screening determines the leading pairing exponent in the controlled high-density limit at fixed separation. At large separation, the pairing scale falls exponentially with squared separation while the instability persists. Extending this result to fixed density assumes Fermi-liquid layers and higher-order dynamical corrections subleading to the static pairing interaction. At high field, we obtain an analytic uniform Hartree-Fock saddle point in the lowest Landau level, coherent at every finite separation. Within Hartree-Fock theory, its finite-wave-vector collective-mode instability favors an excitonic supersolid, distinguishing loss of spatial uniformity from loss of coherence. We conjecture that the quantum Hall bilayer evolves continuously toward weak pairing of composite fermions, with a scale far below the mean-field prediction at large separation. This suppression could produce an apparent critical separation at finite temperature without a ground-state quantum phase transition. The comparison separates the existence, energy scale, and spatial stability of interlayer coherence.

papers.title: A rigid commensurate host and a defect that switches: vacancies in the frustrated alternating spin-(1, 1/2) Heisenberg chain
papers.summary: The alternating spin-$(1,\tfrac12)$ Heisenberg chain with a frustrating next-nearest-neighbor coupling $J_2$ loses its Lieb--Mattis moment through a discontinuous transition to a singlet whose nature was left open. Using an SU(2)-symmetric density-matrix renormalization group, in which the total spin is a quantum-number label, we identify that phase and follow a single vacancy through it. The total spin collapses directly from $S=L/4$ to $S=0$, with no partially polarized window. The singlet phase is critical: its singlet--triplet gap closes as $1/L$, its entanglement entropy grows logarithmically with a central charge $c\simeq1.8$, and its modulation wavevector, extrapolated from $L=80$ to $200$, is commensurate at $3\pi/4$ and independent of $J_2$ to $5\times10^{-5}$. Removing the central $S=1$ site switches the ground state of the doped chain from a triplet to a singlet at $J_2^{\ast}=0.3068(3)$, where the host shows no feature; the triplet is not bound to the vacancy but spread over one of the two segments it leaves. The transmission of correlations through the vacancy saturates at a finite value below $J_2^{\ast}$, $T(\infty)=0.102(15)$ and $0.036(9)$ at $J_2=0.28$ and $0.30$, and the cut-chain law $T\propto L^{-1}$ is excluded on both sides. We also show that the longitudinal correlator is not an observable in a triplet sector.

papers.title: $d$-wave superconductivity in quintuple-layer bulk superconductor La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$
papers.summary: The recent realization of bulk superconductivity in the quintuple-layer nickelate La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$ opens new opportunities to probe the pairing symmetry of the reduced Ruddlesden--Popper (RP) nickelate family. Using an effective five-layer Hubbard model and variational Monte Carlo calculations, we find that a spin-singlet $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave state is energetically favored, while extended-$s$-wave pairing is strongly suppressed. Based on the optimized superconducting state, we further calculate several experimentally accessible observables. The tunneling density of states exhibits a characteristic V-shaped low-energy spectrum, the superfluid density shows a linear low-temperature depletion, the Knight shift decreases below $T_c$, and the spin-lattice relaxation rate follows $1/T_1T\propto T^2$, together providing consistent signatures of a clean nodal superconductor. Extending the same framework to related reduced RP nickelates, we find a robust $d$-wave tendency in infinite-layer LaNiO$_{2}$, while trilayer La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{8}$ at its nominal filling lies close to the boundary between $d$-wave superconductivity and a non-superconducting state. These results establish bulk La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$ as a promising platform for determining the pairing symmetry of nickelate superconductors and suggest a common $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave pairing tendency across the reduced RP nickelate family.

papers.title: Pt-induced semimetallic transport and enhanced thermoelectric response in the half-Heusler alloy YNi_{0.5}Pt_{0.5}Bi
papers.summary: Half-Heusler alloys provide a versatile platform for tuning electronic and thermal transport through chemical substitution. Here, we investigate the thermoelectric and magnetotransport properties of spark-plasma-sintered YNi_{0.5}Pt_{0.5}Bi. Partial substitution of Ni by Pt drives YNiBi toward semimetallic transport, characterized by hole-dominated conduction, a low Hall carrier concentration of $\mathrm{1.9 \times 10^{19} cm^{-3}}$, and a sizeable nonsaturating magnetoresistance of 18$\%$ at 300 K under 14 T. Compared with YNiBi, Pt alloying increases the room-temperature Seebeck coefficient from approximately 90 to 130 $\mathrm{\mu V K^{-1}}$, while reducing the thermal conductivity to 3.15 $\mathrm{W m^{-1} K^{-1}}$. Single-parabolic-band analysis indicates an enhanced carrier effective mass, resulting in a room-temperature power factor of 13.7 $\mathrm{\mu W cm^{-1} K^{-2}}$ and a figure of merit ($zT$= 0.13). First-principles calculations further show a Pt-induced closing of the electronic band gap and a low density of states near the Fermi level, consistent with the experimentally observed semimetal-like transport. These results demonstrate that Ni/Pt alloying provides an effective route for simultaneously tuning the electronic, magnetotransport, and thermoelectric properties of YNiBi-based half-Heusler compounds.

papers.title: Local wave-packet spectroscopy of the Drude weight in Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids
papers.summary: We investigate wave packets generated by a local pulse electric field in a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) with a U(1) charge $q$. Bosonization shows that a local pulse field creates two counterpropagating packets with opposite accumulated charges $\pm qK$ and velocity $v$, where $K$ and $v$ are the TLL parameter and velocity. The packet motion produces a linearly growing charge polarization $P(t)=2 qDt$ in the conducting TLL at non-equilibrium, allowing the Drude weight $D=vK$ to be extracted from real-time local dynamics. We test this local-packet description by time-dependent variational principle simulations of the spin-1/2 XXZ chain. The simulations visualize the density, current, energy, and entanglement profiles in the space-time plane and confirm the predicted packet charge and propagation velocity. We also show that excess energy and entanglement remaining near the pulse region are suppressed in the weak-pulse limit. Finally, the Drude weight obtained from the packet-induced polarization agrees with the exact Bethe-ansatz result, demonstrating local-packet spectroscopy of intrinsic transport in a TLL.

papers.title: Extended strange metal and superconductivity in partially filled moir\'e Hubbard bands
papers.summary: Moir\'e semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. The platform also provides an opportunity to explore the physics of a partially filled Hubbard band at doping densities far away from the Mott insulator, a regime that has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the emergence of an extended strange metal (ESM), in both doping density and twist angle, in a partially filled Hubbard band of twisted bilayer WSe2. The ESM is in the clean limit, persists down to 100mK, and spans over multiple symmetry-breaking ground states; it also appears only at small twist angles, where electronic correlations are strong. These observations distinguish the state from the reported strange metals associated with quantum criticality and favor the viewpoint that it is an intrinsic state of matter. We also report the observation of a new superconducting dome being developed from the ESM but far away from both the Mott insulating state and the van Hove singularity of the material. Our work opens the door to exploring the new regime of partially filled Hubbard bands in the clean limit.

papers.title: From picometre displacements to a three-dimensional lattice gas of polar skyrmions
papers.summary: Polar skyrmions, the electric analogues of magnetic skyrmions, form arrays in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices that are known to be only short-range ordered, but how this disordered ensemble is organized in three dimensions, and how its microscopic structure underlies this organization, have remained largely inaccessible. Here, using three-dimensional difference pair distribution function (3D-{\Delta}PDF) analysis of X-ray diffuse scattering, we show that the polar skyrmion bubbles form a three-dimensional lattice gas: they occupy discrete sites, but their order extends over only a few neighbours and is two to three times stronger across the SrTiO3 spacers than within a layer. This interlayer coupling is consistent with the polarization of the bubbles extending into the spacers. Within each bubble, the polarization rotates in a predominantly N\'eel-type manner, and Pb and Ti rotate together with comparable picometre displacements, demonstrating that both A- and B-site cations take part in the polar distortion.

papers.title: Parafermions in polarized $\nu=2/3$ Fractional Quantum (Anomalous) Hall Heterostructures
papers.summary: Motivated by recent experimental signatures of fractional Chern insulators in 2D quantum materials, we investigate the realization of $\mathbb Z_3$ parafermion zero modes (PZMs) on edges of spin-polarized $\nu=2/3$ fractional quantum Hall states which are proximitized by superconductors. Unlike the spin-unpolarized Halperin state, the polarized $\nu=2/3$ edge contains counterpropagating electron and fractional quasihole modes, giving rise to a plethora of competing tunneling and pairing processes. We focus on the vicinity of the fixed point where these modes reorganize into decoupled charge and neutral sectors, with the neutral sector describing an emergent dipole degree of freedom. Using bosonization and renormalization group analysis, we lay out the parameter space in which the interedge dipole interactions gap the neutral sector to stabilize one dominant tunneling and one dominant pairing channel resulting in a double sine-Gordon model in the charge sector which supports $\mathbb{Z}_3$ PZMs at domain walls. We discuss both clean and disordered systems. In clean systems this mechanism requires a certain degree of control of the interaction strength and range. In contrast, disorder can provide a more generic route: While short-ranged, edge-uncorrelated disorder % on the two edges suppresses the simultaneous pinning required for stable parafermion modes, when the disorder on the two edges is sufficiently correlated, as expected for smooth disorder potentials, the parameter regime hosting PZMs increases.

papers.title: Band-Resolved Superconducting Gaps via the Thermal Hall Effect in CeRu2
papers.summary: Standard bulk probes of multiband superconductors cannot assign pairing gaps to specific electron or hole Fermi surfaces. Here we show that thermal Hall transport ($\kappa_{xy}$), constrained by specific heat and normal-state magnetotransport, resolves this ambiguity in the compensated heavy-fermion superconductor CeRu$_2$. Fixing the gap magnitudes ($\Delta_e/k_B\approx 13$K, $\Delta_h/k_B\approx 8$K) and band mobilities completely determines the electronic degrees of freedom in $\kappa_{xx}$ and $\kappa_{xy}$. A low-field sign reversal in $\kappa_{xy}$ places the larger gap on the heavy Ce $4f$ electron sheets and the smaller on the hole sheets.

papers.title: Information-Theoretic Limits for Rectangular Spiked Matrix Models with Rotationally Invariant Noise
papers.summary: We study the information-theoretic limits of inference in rectangular rank-one spiked matrix models with additive rotationally invariant noise, thereby going beyond the standard assumption of independent noise entries. Using the replica method from statistical physics, we derive a variational formula for the mutual information between the signal and the data, together with a system of saddle point equations predicting the minimum mean squared error in estimating the rank-one spike. We further show that, in the Bayes-optimal setting, these saddle point equations coincide with the fixed point equations of the state evolution of a recently proposed orthogonal approximate message passing algorithm with Bayes-optimal denoisers. This equivalence provides an algorithmic interpretation of the replica prediction and supports the Bayes-optimality of orthogonal approximate message passing whenever the relevant fixed point is unique. Numerical evaluations of the saddle point equations for several rotationally invariant noise ensembles and signal priors, together with finite-size simulations of the algorithm, confirm the asymptotic predictions. They illustrate both regimes with a unique informative fixed point, where orthogonal approximate message passing is predicted to attain the minimum mean squared error, and regimes with multiple fixed points, where a statistical-to-computational gap exists.

papers.title: Quantum Work Statistics from Entanglement-Assisted Invariance
papers.summary: We demonstrate that the one-time measurement scheme is more consistent than the standard two-time measurement scheme with respect to the fundamental symmetry of entanglement, namely entanglement-assisted invariance (envariance). In particular, the work statistics obtained from the one-time measurement scheme arise naturally as a direct consequence of envariance for any driving unitary, without involving an explicit measurement postulate, whereas the analogous identification for the two-time measurement scheme is possible only for a Haar-measure-zero set of unitaries. This envariance-based formulation eliminates the ambiguity in work statistics related to the energetic cost of measurement.

papers.title: Equality of the Jellium and the Uniform Electron Gas Energies

papers.title: Vision-Guided Closed-Loop Autonomous Navigation of Light-Driven Janus Microbots
papers.summary: Artificial microbots capable of precise and autonomous navigation could provide versatile platforms for microscale transport, manipulation, and task execution in complex environments. However, reliable navigation becomes increasingly challenging at the micrometre scale, particularly when the surrounding environment changes dynamically. Here, we develop a vision-guided closed-loop navigation framework for light-driven cube-shaped hematite/TiO2 Janus microbots with a characteristic size of approximately 3 {\mu}m. Real-time visual localization using a custom-trained YOLOv11 object-detection model is integrated with discretized waypoint-based magnetic steering to enable precise navigation along complex prescribed trajectories, with more than 90% of the measured trajectory deviations remaining below 6 {\mu}m across the tested path geometries. The framework further enables arbitrary user-defined free-hand trajectories and autonomous navigation through a physically confined maze. In dynamically changing environments, A* path planning enables real-time path replanning while avoiding multiple independently swimming 5 {\mu}m spherical Janus micromotors. Finally, the microbot selectively captures multiple cargo particles and autonomously transports and delivers them to a predefined location while simultaneously avoiding dynamic obstacles. These results establish an integrated platform combining programmable trajectory control, autonomous path planning, real-time environmental adaptation, and task execution within a single light-driven Janus microbot system.

papers.title: Dark Matter Axions Modulate Dark State Scintillation
papers.summary: The decay rate of the thallium-iodine dark state in the popular alkali-halide scintillator NaI(Tl) modulates in phase with the dipole anisotropy of the cosmic microwave background (CMB), it is argued. Axion dark matter particles --- at rest in the local CMB rest-frame --- couple to the static magnetic field created in their rest-frame by the static electric quadrupole field within the tetragonally-distorted thallium-iodine octahedron surrounding each dark state. For axions with rest-mass energy near the roughly 0.5 eV dark state activation energy in NaI(Tl), the resulting near-infrared electric field created by this axion electrodynamic interaction modulates the dark state scintillation lifetime by bringing home the excited hole --- from the four in-plane iodine 5p orbitals that share it --- to the Tl 6s shell where it can recombine with the excited Tl 6p electron to produce the scintillation light.

papers.title: Dynamic Coarse-Graining of Linear and Non-Linear Systems: Mori-Zwanzig Formalism and Beyond
papers.summary: To investigate the impact of non-linear interactions on dynamic coarse graining, we study a simplified model system, featuring a tracer particle in a complex environment. Using a projection operator formalism and computer simulations, we systematically derive generalized Langevin equations (GLEs) describing the dynamics of this particle. We compare different kinds of linear and non-linear coarse-graining procedures to understand how non-linearities enter reconstructed generalized Langevin equations and how they influence the coarse-grained dynamics. For non-linear external potentials, we show analytically and numerically that the non-Gaussian parameter and the incoherent intermediate scattering function will not be correctly reproduced by the GLE if a linear projection is applied. This, however, can be overcome by using non-linear projection operators. We also study anharmonic coupling between the tracer and the environment and demonstrate that the reconstructed memory kernel develops an additional trap-dependent contribution. Our study highlights some open challenges and possible solutions in dynamic coarse graining.

papers.title: Theory of phonon angular momentum transport across a smooth crystal interface
papers.summary: We theoretically elucidate the transfer of phonon angular momentum by acoustic modes across a smooth interface between crystals. We analyze this process, which is difficult to describe with the conventional acoustic mismatch model, using a reformulated boundary condition and the Boltzmann theory. For an interface between a chiral and an achiral crystal, our analysis reveals that thermal gradients in the chiral crystal induce angular momentum, which diffuses into the achiral crystal even without heat flow. Notably, within an approximation retaining the chirality-induced population imbalance, the density of angular momentum can be enhanced near the interface. These findings advance our understanding of phonon transport and its interplay with electron spins.

papers.title: Dirac Representation for Lattice Spin Operators: Spin-$1/2$ and Spin-$1$ cases
papers.summary: We introduce a quantum representation of lattice spin operators (LSOs) by mapping quantum spins to their classical analogues for spin values $S=1/2$ and $S=1$. The resulting Dirac (bra--ket) forms are derived from the structure of binary and ternary digit distributions in non-negative integers. \color{blue} The construction requires only an enumeration of the lattice sites and is therefore independent on the spatial dimension and lattice geometry. \color{black} Analytical expressions for extracting the $j$th bit or trit of an integer without performing an explicit binary or ternary decomposition are obtained. \color{blue}As an application of the representation, \color{black} we analyze the one-dimensional spin-$1/2$ {XXZ} Heisenberg model with open boundaries in a magnetic field in both absence (uniform magnetic field) and presence of disorder (random magnetic field). In the absence of disorder (clean system), we demonstrate that the corresponding eigenvalue problem can be reduced to a tight-binding problem on a graph. For the isotropic case, this is solved analytically without resorting to any spinless transformation or the Bethe Ansatz. In the presence of disorder, a convergent perturbation theory is elaborated. Our analytical results are benchmarked against exact diagonalization for systems up to $K\leq 18$ spins. These computations exploit the global $U(1)$ symmetry to block-diagonalize the Hamiltonian and the spin-inversion symmetry to further decompose the zero-magnetization sector. Quantitative agreement between analytical and numerical results is observed.

papers.title: Data-Driven Thiele Equation Approach for State-Dependent Coefficients in the Nonlinear Dynamics of Vortex-based Nano-Oscillators
papers.summary: Spin-torque vortex oscillators provide a model system for the nonlinear dynamics of a confined magnetic texture. Their motion is commonly described by the Thiele equation, but its standard form keeps the gyrovector and damping tensor fixed at their rigid-vortex values and becomes inaccurate at large gyration amplitudes. We introduce a data-driven Thiele equation approach that extracts effective, position-dependent Thiele coefficients from a single current-ramp micromagnetic simulation by interpolating the magnetization in vortex-core-position space. The extracted maps reveal a weak increase of the gyrovector magnitude and a pronounced separation of the radial and azimuthal dissipation as the orbit expands, providing quantitative signatures of confinement-and motion-induced vortex deformation. Because the gyrotropic, dissipative, conservative, and spin-transfer contributions retain their usual Thiele structure, the resulting description remains physically interpretable rather than acting as a black-box surrogate. Incorporating these state-dependent coefficients into the equation reproduces the nonlinear stable-orbit dynamics and accurately predicts the response to time-varying currents, whereas a conventional constant-coefficient description predicts vortex expulsion. The framework therefore provides a systematic route for deriving effective collective-coordinate dynamics from full micromagnetic states with high computational efficiency.

papers.title: Spontaneous and Collective Learning in a Minimal Agent-Environment Model
papers.summary: How can information be extracted from data without explicit guidance or rewards? We investigate this question in a minimal setting where a classifying agent is exposed to a stream of structured data produced by a generative environment, and evolves by seeking consistency of its own labels in time. We find that imposing a simplicity bias on the classification rule can drive the dynamics toward label-coherent steady states, which we coin functional replicators. Remarkably, these persistent labeling rules align with the latent structure of the data. Using analytical tools from statistical mechanics, we characterize this spontaneous learning phase transition. Extending the analysis to a collective of agents that pool labels from one another, we show that interaction reshapes the learning phase boundary, in some regimes enabling spontaneous learning that no isolated agent can achieve, while suppressing it in others. Our minimal framework thus opens a route to decentralized learning through label exchange alone, requiring no access to the internal weights of other agents.

papers.title: Optimal active engines obey the thermodynamic Lorentz force law
papers.summary: What are the fundamental limitations for finite-time engines that extract work from active nonequilibrium systems, and what are the optimal protocols that approach them? We show that the finite-time work extraction for nonconservative overdamped Langevin systems may be rewritten as a Lorentz force Lagrangian action, with the kinetic term corresponding to a thermodynamic metric term that is an $L_2$-optimal transport cost for the time-dependent probability density, and the magnetic field coupling term corresponding to an effective quasistatic work extraction, proving that optimal protocols counterdiabatically steer the thermodynamic state trajectory to satisfy a Lorentz force law defined on thermodynamic state space. We utilize and reinterpret classic concepts from electromagnetism in the setting of cyclical nonequilibrium processes. We show that the housekeeping heat can be controlled to be arbitrarily close to zero by minimizing nonequilibrium fluctuations. It immediately follows from our results that the constant-velocity angle clamp protocol applied to the $F_1$ molecular motor in a recent experiment [T. Mishima et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 148402 (2025)] is in fact the globally optimal protocol: it produces zero housekeeping heat while simultaneously minimizing dissipation and maximizing work transduction.

papers.title: Quantum geometry, localization, and topological bounds of spin fluctuations
papers.summary: We study how topological crystalline defects--dislocations--reshape the real-space quantum geometric tensor and act as tunable sources of quantum geometry. We show that dislocations strongly enhance the quantum metric, establishing a direct link between lattice topology and the Hilbert-space geometry of states. We characterize the quantum geometry of topological magnons in ordered arrays of dislocations, demonstrating that defect-induced geometric enhancement controls their localization and topological protection. In disordered arrays, dislocation-driven geometry expands the accessible topological phase space and enables transitions to disorder-induced topological phases. Our results identify the quantum metric as a tunable bridge between crystalline topology, magnonic excitations, and emergent topological matter in aperiodic solid-state and synthetic systems.

papers.title: Boundary condition for phonon distribution functions at a smooth crystal interface and interfacial angular momentum transfer
papers.summary: We theoretically elucidate the boundary conditions for phonon distribution functions of long-wavelength acoustic phonons at smooth crystal interfaces. We first derive boundary conditions that fully incorporate reflection, transmission, and mode conversion. We obtain these conditions for phonons from those for classical lattice vibrations, using the correspondence between the quantum and classical descriptions. This formulation provides a theoretical foundation for the acoustic mismatch model, widely used to analyze Kapitza resistance. We then refine the boundary conditions to include spatial dependence parallel to the interface. The refined form captures transverse shifts of elastic wave packets, analogous to the optical Imbert--Fedorov shift, and ensures conservation of total angular momentum. Consequently, circularly polarized phonons carrying spin angular momentum (SAM) generate phonon orbital angular momentum (OAM) at the interface. We analytically determine the spatial profile of this OAM and demonstrate that SAM and OAM are both involved in the interfacial diffusion of chiral phonons. Our theory provides concise boundary conditions for phonons, with applications ranging from heat transport to phonon angular momentum transport.

papers.title: Superconducting properties of transition metal dichalcogenides in proximity to a conventional superconductor
papers.summary: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) hold relevance for spin-triplet superconducting phases due to their inherent Ising spin-orbit coupling, but the majority of studies have so far focused on oversimplified models. In this work, we consider a TMD monolayer using a three-orbital model with anisotropic couplings and investigate the emergent superconducting properties when it is placed in proximity to a conventional spin-singlet $s$-wave superconductor. We find that the multiorbital nature of the TMDs lead to superconducting gaps not only at zero energy but also at higher energies, so-called hybridization gaps, which exhibit a complex structure due to the anisotropic couplings, challenging their spectral measurement. Moreover, we find that the inherent Ising spin-orbit coupling induces a spin splitting and a spin polarization along the $z$ direction, which correlates with the emergence of mixed spin-triplet superconducting pairs. These spin-triplet pair correlations appear in the monolayer as a proximity-induced effect due to the impact of the Ising spin-orbit field on conventional spin-singlet $s$-wave superconductivity. Taking realistic parameters for a $\text{MoS}_2$ monolayer, we show that the Ising field is strong enough to induce spin-triplet pair correlations of the same magnitude as their spin-singlet counterparts. We also include Rashba spin-orbit coupling, naturally emerging in a heterostructure and find that it induces equal spin-triplet superconducting pairs that compete with the mixed spin-triplet pairs induced by the Ising spin-orbit coupling. Our findings help understand the superconducting properties of TMDs in proximity to conventional superconductors.

papers.title: Signatures of Dynes superconductivity in the THz response of ALD-grown NbN thin films
papers.summary: The frequency-dependent complex optical conductivity reflects key properties of superconductors, such as the energy gap in the density of states (DOS) and the superfluid density. For disordered superconductors, the optical conductivity often can be described within Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) theory, while in corresponding tunneling experiments, deviations in the observed DOS typically require modelling by the phenomenological Dynes formula. The implications of such Dynes DOS for optics were rarely discussed so far. Here we probe the terahertz conductivity of superconducting NbN thin films with thicknesses ranging from 4.5 to 20nm, which were grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD). Our frequency range from 0.3 to 2.1 THz covers energies below and above the spectral gap. For 20nm thick NbN, we find in the optical conductivity distinct deviations from the BCS model, including a step-like characteristic in the absorption at half the zero-temperature spectral gap. These observations can be fully captured by Dynes electrodynamics with a small and temperature-independent pair-breaking rate. For the other films, we also observe signs of Dynes electrodynamics, and we discuss the evolution of the energy gap, the superfluid density, and the pair-breaking rate as function of film thickness.

papers.title: Anomalous Thermal Conductivity Reversal Driven by a Fluctuating Charge Density Wave
papers.summary: For more than a century, the lattice thermal conductivity of crystalline solids has been known to decrease with increasing temperature, as the phonons that carry heat scatter more strongly via Umklapp processes. Here we report a pronounced violation of this rule in the layered charge-density-wave (CDW) metal 2H-TaSe2. Its in-plane thermal conductivity is strongly nonmonotonic: it peaks sharply at the 122 K ordering transition, collapses to a deep minimum near 210 K, and then anomalously reverses, rising with temperature to at least 350 K. Such a high-temperature reversal, in which a crystal conducts heat more efficiently as it is heated, is rare in crystalline solids. Its thermal conductivity minimum lies deep in the disordered phase well above the ordering transition, unlike the weak, transition-centered anomalies of other charge-density-wave systems, pointing to heat conduction governed by fluctuating rather than established order. Combining inelastic X-ray scattering, selected-area electron diffraction, and synchrotron X-ray diffraction, we attribute the reversal to phonons scattering off persistent, fluctuating charge order that survives more than 150 K above the long-range transition, to at least 300 K. A phenomenological phonon-CDW scattering model, tied directly to the measured diffraction linewidth and intensity, quantitatively reproduces the entire nonmonotonic curve. We also reveal that the charge order melts not abruptly but through a fluctuation- and defect-driven, weak first-order process, leaving short-range correlations far above the transition. This work establishes fluctuating charge order as a sensitive control knob for thermal transport in quantum materials and thermal conductivity as a powerful probe of the hidden charge order.

papers.title: Density and shape govern the dynamical self-organization of active matter on a closed surface
papers.summary: Morphogenesis emerges from dynamic feedback among geometry, mechanics, and chemistry; however, disentangling these contributions in living systems remains challenging. Here, we focus on the interplay between geometry and mechanics by developing a minimal in vitro model in which purified microtubules and kinesin motor clusters self-organize into a two-dimensional active nematic cortex at the surface of spherical water-in-oil droplets. The spherical geometry enforces a total topological charge of +2, here realized by four +1/2 defects whose trajectories reveal robust, self-sustained oscillations. Using full-surface reconstructions, we show that the collective dynamics of the defects lead to a periodic switching between planar and tetrahedral arrangements through alternating coiling and hemisphere-crossing phases. By tuning microtubule density, the system spans a continuum from a classic defect-dominated active nematic to a regime resembling an extensile filament confined to a curved surface, where low density is associated with increased trajectory variability and direction reversals. Geometric perturbations introduced through controlled squeezing redistribute curvature and induce the nucleation of additional defects, thereby reorganizing the entire topological landscape while preserving total charge. Together, these results show that periodic morphogenetic-like cycles, defect topology, and material organization can arise solely from the interplay of activity, density, and curvature. This reconstituted system provides a versatile platform for elucidating the coupling between mechanics and geometry underlying shape formation in active biological matter.

papers.title: Exact dynamics and dimensional effects in torque-driven trapped active Brownian particles
papers.summary: The interplay of chirality, self-propulsion, and confinement generates pronounced non-equilibrium fluctuations, with higher-order moments encoding the shape of the position distribution. We present an exact analytical framework, based on the Laplace transform of the Fokker-Planck equation, for the transient dynamics of a chiral active Brownian particle in a harmonic trap in two and three dimensions. Closed-form expressions for time-dependent moments up to fourth order allow a full characterization of the excess kurtosis across transient and steady-state regimes. In two dimensions, the excess kurtosis exhibits damped oscillations with multiple re-entrant crossovers, evolving from negative values, indicative of off-centered ring-like distributions, to small positive values characteristic of near-Gaussian distributions with a weak tail enhancement; increasing trap stiffness progressively suppresses this oscillatory response. In three dimensions, the excess kurtosis of a torque-driven active Brownian particle stays negative, reflecting robust non-Gaussian fluctuations with half-ring- to band-like position distributions in the plane defined by the torque axis. These results reveal how chirality, propulsion, confinement, and dimensionality jointly shape transient dynamics and provide experimentally accessible signatures of confined chiral active motion.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights into the spatial organization of RNA polymerase proteins and the chromosome in E. coli cells
papers.summary: Along the bacterial chromosome, regions called rrn operons contain genes that are transcribed into ribosomal RNA. These operons are among the most transcriptionally active sites in the genome. It has been observed in E. coli that RNA polymerase (RNAP), while binding to these genetic loci along the chromosome during transcription, forms dense clusters, leading to spatial colocalization of the operons within the cell. Recent experimental evidence suggests that liquid-liquid phase separation contributes to the formation of RNAP clusters, with the antitermination factor NusA playing a key role. We present a simulation model to investigate the mechanisms underlying the formation of these biomolecular condensates. We propose that mutual attraction between NusA proteins, which exhibit a miscibility gap at higher concentrations, drives condensate formation via a polymer-assisted condensation pathway, and we demonstrate how these condensates promote the colocalization of rrn operons. Our results reconcile seemingly disparate experimental observations of chromosomal organization reported in fluorescence-based imaging and Hi-C experiments.

papers.title: Bulk-dissociated topological bands without spin-orbit coupling in hetero-dimensional superconducting metamaterials
papers.summary: Topological superconductors (TSCs) in superconducting hybrid heterostructures, which integrate superconducting and non-superconducting materials, have been intensely investigated with the hope of discovering exotic non-Abelian anyons for fault-tolerant quantum computing. In this effort, a challenge for hybrid superconducting systems is controlling hybridization, which is often a balance between enhancing the superconducting proximity effect at the cost of suppressing desirable electronic properties such as strong spin-orbit interactions. Hence, discovering hybrid superconducting systems with topological properties controlled and enhanced by material geometry design without spin-orbit interactions would be intriguing to explore. In this work, we theoretically study a square superconducting network decorated with spin-polarized magnetic adatoms. We find that localized Yu-Shiba-Rusinov bound states at magnetic adatom sites collectively form a weak topological superconducting phase despite the absence of spin-orbit interactions. We then demonstrate that by tuning the Fermi energy of the network, the system can transition from a weak TSC phase to a bulk-dissociated TSC phase where the edge state bands separate from the bulk, giving rise to unexpected features such as nodal lines and co-existing bulk-dissociated edge and corner modes. Moreover, our findings highlight how hetero-dimensional superconducting metamaterials can serve as a useful template for controlling the coupling and dissociation between electronic degrees of freedom of different dimensionalities.

papers.title: Limits of the Non-Linear Generalized Langevin Equation: Cross-Correlations, Irreversibility and Desynchronization
papers.summary: The generalized Langevin equation (GLE) is widely used to model complex soft-matter systems, including biomolecular dynamics, by incorporating memory effects and colored noise into coarse-grained descriptions. However, recent results suggest that combining memory with non-linear forces, ubiquitous in soft matter, introduces fundamental analytical inconsistencies. Here, using a simplified model, we investigate the practical numerical consequences of these analytical results. We show that non-linear forces generate cross-correlations with the noise, modifying the fluctuation-dissipation theorem and rendering the noise position-dependent and irreversible. This implies that the commonly assumed reversible Gaussian noise in GLE simulations fails to capture essential features of the microscopic fluctuations. For weak non-linearities, these issues can be partially resolved either by using an iterative optimization of memory or by using microscopically consistent noise, which unexpectedly synchronizes GLE trajectories with the underlying microscopic dynamics. For stronger non-linearities like high barriers or shoulders in the external potential, however, iterative reconstruction fails and we observe desynchronization, indicating that the non-linear GLE no longer correctly reproduces the microscopic dynamics. Our results show in which situations non-linear GLEs can be accurately applied and when they fail, thus providing practical guidance for their application to coarse-grain soft-matter systems.

papers.title: Spin effects in the particle current of Bose-Einstein condensates in synthetic gauge fields
papers.summary: Spin reveals the rotational features of a system independently of its state of motion. Hence, it is not a relativistic quantity, despite giving rise to effects that emerge naturally from relativistic equations only. Within a non-relativistic framework these effects are not inherently captured, and have to be added by resorting to symmetry principles or to the asymptotic limit of the corresponding relativistic framework. We report on one of these effects: the divergenceless spin term in the particle current density of spinor Bose-Einstein condensates. It could be observed in the setup of a synthetic Hall system made with non-relativistic pseudospin-1/2 bosonic particles. By tuning the interaction strength, the system can show how the spin term in the particle current is needed for the local matching of classical drift velocity in the ground state of the non-interacting system, whereas for increasing interparticle interactions the spin-to-orbital current ratio decreases. In either case, since the overall particle velocity changes with the spin term contribution, so does its circulation in a loop, which in turn has physical consequences for its relationship with the Aharonov-Bohm phase shift.

papers.title: On representation of macroscopic crack in periodic fine-scale discrete mechanical models
papers.summary: In multiscale modeling of heterogeneous softening materials, boundary conditions (BC) in the fine-scale model strongly influence the strain localization pattern and the macroscopic response. For rectilinear models (e.g., squares or cubes), standard Periodic BCs produce artificially ductile behavior with excessive energy dissipation when the localization band inclination does not match the periodicity directions. Recently proposed Tessellation and Percolation-path-aligned BCs promise to address this by adapting the periodicity frame to align with the evolving localization bands. Alternatively, spherical/circular models provide an orientation independent response by design. Unfortunately, the standard Periodic BCs do not allow development of proper localization band crossing spherical model's boundaries. A recently proposed modification addresses this by adding a displacement jump to the spherical periodic BCs. This study evaluates the applicability of these novel BCs to a mesoscale discrete particle model of concrete. Two-dimensional square and circular models under uniaxial tension with different loading directions are analyzed, with the selected approaches extended to three-dimensional cube models. Results show that Percolation-path-aligned BCs exhibit major shortcomings: they can lead to multiple localization bands due to uneven straining of the two boundary sections and their weakly constrained section can be prone to spurious strain localization. In contrast, Tessellation BCs consistently yield a well-defined localization band, whose length is determined solely by the model geometry, making it straightforward to account for in post-processing. Periodic boundary conditions augmented with a displacement jump applied to a circular model sometimes incorrect produce crack patterns similar to those under the standard Periodic BCs.

papers.title: Symmetry and Quantum Geometry in Bloch Bands
papers.summary: Quantum geometric quantities have featured heavily in the discussion of the properties of quantum systems in recent years. Among quantities most commonly discussed is the variance of Berry curvature and the integral of the trace of the quantum metric tensor. Despite their usefulness, it is known that they suffer from one significant complication: for a tight-binding model, the quantum geometric quantities depend not only on the parameters of the tight-binding model itself, but also the real space geometry of the tight-binding model, the so-called "orbital embedding". One explicitly geometry-independent quantity is therefore the minimal value of the quantum geometric quantity out of all possible real space geometries. In this work, we demonstrate that, if the tight-binding model is compatible with certain spatial symmetries, then the real space geometry that minimizes the variance of the Berry curvature or the integral of the trace of the quantum metric tensor must obey all those spatial symmetries. We further show that the statement is applicable to systems with magnetic translation symmetries and other composite symmetries, with implications for the quantum geometry of the Hofstadter model.

These Janus structures exhibit significant spin-splittingelectronic states, large topological band gaps (51.4 meV) and high N\'eel temperatures (415 K). We further reveal that valley polarization can be effectively tuned via applied in-plane strain and the resulting valley-polarized anomalous Hall conductivity can be manipulated by shifting the Fermi level. Our work suggests a new strategy based on altermagnetism for engineering spin-splitting states in superconducting systems and inspires further exploration of superconducting spintronics.

papers.title: Experimental Observation of Mesoscopic Dynamic Fluctuations in Water-Alcohol Mixtures
papers.summary: We applied a dynamic fluctuation measurement method to liquid water-methanol mixtures over a wide range of compositions and temperatures. This method, which we developed in recent years, combines ultrasonic and inelastic X-ray scattering techniques to detect mesoscopic-level fluctuations - that is, the degree of heterogeneity - in liquids using sound waves. As a result, it was found that dynamic fluctuations exist across a wide range of compositions and temperatures, including pure substances (water and methanol). Furthermore, in the low-methanol composition range (approximately 20% mol or less), the strength of dynamic fluctuation increased toward lower compositions and lower temperatures, suggesting that the origin of the fluctuation lies in the low temperature (supercooled) region of water alone. Conversely, this indicates that in the range below 20% methanol, fluctuations in water alone are dominant rather than the mixed effects of water and methanol. We performed similar dynamic fluctuation measurements on water-ethanol and water-glycerol mixtures at room temperature. We found that dynamic fluctuations exist universally across the entire composition range, and confirmed an increase in the strength of dynamic fluctuations toward lower compositions in the regions approximately below 15% and below 20%, respectively. This revealed that the phenomenon is not unique to methanol systems but is a common behavior shared by water-alcohol mixtures. It has long been known that water-alcohol mixtures exhibit various thermodynamic anomalies, but the mechanisms behind them have not yet been fully elucidated. The present results are expected to provide a new direction for discussion on this issue.

papers.title: Superconductivity in a Bulk Moire Superlattice Material
papers.summary: Moire materials provide a versatile platform realizing emergent electronic states arising from enhanced correlation due to flat bands. A variety of phenomena including superconductivity, low dimensional ferromagnetism, Mott insulating phase, and topological phenomena have been reported in such systems. To date, moire phenomena have been predominantly explored in artificially assembled low dimensional van der Waals structures, where relative twist and lattice alignment are controlled during device fabrication. Recently, intrinsically grown bulk moire crystals have emerged as a complementary materials platform, in which lattice mismatch between constituent layers generates a coherent moire superlattice throughout the bulk crystal. Here, we report the evidence of bulk superconductivity in single crystals of a recently reported bulk Moire material [Sr6TaS8]1+x[TaS2]8 at ambient pressure. The material exhibits a bulk superconducting transition at Tc = 2.5 K, evidenced consistently by electrical transport, magnetic susceptibility, and heat capacity measurements on single crystals. Structural characterization by X-ray diffraction and atomic resolution electron microscopy establishes the composite, incommensurate crystal structure and scanning tunnelling microscopy reveals a long-wavelength surface modulation due to the incommensurate structure. The observation of bulk superconductivity establishes superconductivity as an emergent phase in this intrinsically synthesized moire material and highlights bulk moire crystals as a promising platform for investigating correlated quantum phenomena beyond artificially assembled two-dimensional structures.

papers.title: Low temperature thermodynamics of $S_{\mathrm{eff}}=1/2$ triangular lattice quantum spin liquid candidate TlYbS$_2$
papers.summary: Geometrically frustrated triangular-lattice antiferromagnets exhibit a delicate competition between magnetic order and quantum spin liquid (QSL) behavior, with the Yb-based delafossite family $A$Yb$X_2$ providing a structurally clean platform for exploring this physics. Here, we report a comprehensive study of single-crystal TlYbS$_2$ using DC magnetization, AC susceptibility, electron spin resonance (ESR), and specific heat measurements extending from room temperature to the millikelvin regime. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirms a trigonal $R\bar{3}m$ structure comprising well-separated triangular layers of Yb$^{3+}$ ions with no detectable site disorder. At zero field, a weak thermodynamic anomaly is observed near $530$ mK, which may indicate the onset of a weakly ordered state similar to that reported in KYbSe$_2$. Below $300$ mK, the zero-field magnetic specific heat follows $C_{\rm m}\propto T^{1.8}$, close to a quadratic temperature dependence, in contrast to the linear temperature dependence reported for the sister compound TlYbSe$_2$, which has been described in terms of the interplay between spinons and thermally excited gauge-flux excitations. Magnetization and ESR measurements establish pronounced easy-plane magnetic anisotropy, with $g_\perp/g_\parallel \approx 6.9$. The anomaly near $530$ mK exhibits a strongly anisotropic response to magnetic field. For $H\perp c$, it remains visible up to approximately $2$ T and continuously evolves toward a field-induced ordered phase above approximately $2.5$ T, followed by a sequence of field-induced phases that includes a $1/3$ magnetization plateau between approximately $5$ and $8$ T and full polarization near $17$ T. In contrast, for $H\parallel c$, the anomaly weakens and is suppressed near $3$ T, consistent with the recently reported confinement--deconfinement transition from an ordered state to a field-induced QSL.

papers.title: Knowledge-Guided Construction of Machine Learning Potentials for Reactive Behavior in Energetic Materials
papers.summary: Energetic materials involve multiple interactions, making reliable machine-learning potentials (MLPs) difficult to construct without extensive datasets. Here, we enhance the ability of the neural network interatomic potential (NNAP) to describe molecular systems using sphmulti, a refined spherical-harmonic basis set that combines extra radial basis with element-specific chemical weighting in each radial channel. We further integrate hyperactive learning, farthest-point sampling, and iterative sufficiency criteria with knowledge-guided key events, enabling the NNAP to retain essential information for describing the material system. For 3,3'-diamino-4,4'-azoxyfurazan, the resulting NNAP is trained on only 13,680 configurations yet captures key properties, including the isomerization barrier, pyrolysis activation energy, and shock Hugoniot behavior. NNAP-driven molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that pyrolysis proceeds through furazan-ring opening followed by chain reactions, whereas shock loading induces anisotropic hydrogen transfer driven by interlayer structural deformations. This work enables efficient and reliable MLPs for energetic materials.

papers.title: Cooperative Boundary Switching of Mesoscopic Real Spectra in a Non-Hermitian Chain Family
papers.summary: At fixed bulk criticality, every fixed nonsingular real single-end potential preserves a growing local population of real eigenvalues in an open analytic family of non-Hermitian chains. An open region of two-end real potentials removes this population. A boundary-amplitude criterion fixes the minimum number of controlled ends. The population grows as $\sqrt N$, where $N$ is chain length, although its normalized spectral weight vanishes and the local limiting bands remain unchanged. For a representative chain's four zero-detuning settings, an independent passive Hermitian double chain converts this distinction into separated resonances at one fixed local port under a common coupling scan at fixed probe carrier. Its absolute reflection contrast and stability margin both scale as $N^{-1}$, with explicit sufficient resource budgets. Boundary amplitudes thus fix a minimum control requirement that limiting bands and thermodynamic spectral density do not specify.

papers.title: Room-Temperature Metallic 2D Ferromagnetism Stabilized by Quantum Metric
papers.summary: The recent discovery of long-sought dice-lattice bands in layered electride YCl opens up unprecedented opportunities for studying correlated electrons in real dice lattice systems. While the weakly dispersive band at the Fermi level is partially filled and density-wave states are expected due to Fermi surface nesting based on conventional theories, the ARPES measurement nevertheless revealed a uniform flat band splitting of 0.5 eV, suggesting unusual ferromagnetism (FM) borne out of the metallic 2D dice lattice. In this Letter, we propose that the uniform metallic FM order is stabilized by the prominent quantum metric near topological band crossing points at K and K', which reconstructs the magnetic instability in the dice metal and tips the density-wave instability toward a uniform FM order. Importantly, our analysis based on random phase approximation (RPA) and Hartree-Fock theory predicts a remarkably high Curie temperature above room temperature for the 2D FM order. These findings establish the first example of a room-temperature 2D metallic magnet stabilized by quantum metric, which not only exemplifies the fundamental significance of quantum geometry in solids but also bears far-reaching applications in energy-efficient high-density magnetic memories.

papers.title: Orbitronics in Zero-dimensional Graphene Nanoflakes via Electrode Coupling
papers.summary: We show that graphene nanoflakes realize a previously unexplored form of orbitronics in which orbital currents emerge in the absence of intrinsic angular momentum of the constituent atoms. Starting with a hexagonal graphene nanoflake, we demonstrate the presence of energy-degenerate eigenstates with opposite non-zero expectation values of the angular momentum. Placing electrodes in an appropriate configuration on the flake couples the reservoirs more strongly to one of the two opposite-angular-momentum states, yielding a chiral current that carries a net orbital angular momentum. The resulting circulating orbital currents generate magnetic fringe fields that are experimentally accessible with spin centers or superconducting quantum interference magnetometers, providing avenues for their experimental realization. Finally, our work establishes a new platform for exploring and studying orbitronics in zero-dimensional systems.

papers.title: Uniform Bessel bounds for magnetization crossings in finite Ising chains
papers.summary: In a finite zero-field Ising chain, the all-up configuration and zero magnetization become equally likely at a single coupling. This crossing has recently been described as a thermal transition of the finite chain, an analogue of a first-order transition temperature, and approximated by an analytic estimate and a numerical fit. We find its asymptotics, with explicit constants, for free and for periodic ends. The coupling at the crossing grows like half the logarithm of the length of the chain, minus half the logarithm of that logarithm. So the correlation length at the crossing is a vanishing fraction of the chain. Periodic ends lower the coupling at the crossing by an amount that decays like the inverse logarithm of the length. The earlier approximations lack the doubly logarithmic term, which explains why a fit on chains of moderate length finds a slope below one half. The proofs treat the magnetization as the position of a persistent random walk and compare its central probability with a modified Bessel function, with a relative error bound that is explicit for every length. For free ends this traps the crossing in an explicit interval at every length. The proof is analytic for long chains and uses exact integer arithmetic for short ones. We also locate, for each smaller magnetization, the coupling at which it becomes as likely as full magnetization.

papers.title: Airway cross-sectional area measurement using quantitative endoscopy with AI-enabled depth estimation: A proof-of-concept study
papers.summary: Endoscopy is widely used in medicine to visualize anatomical structures for diagnosis and treatment evaluation. However, it does not currently allow rapid, quantitative measurement of airway cross-sectional area (CSA), a key metric for diagnosing and managing respiratory pathologies. There is growing interest in AI-enabled quantitative endoscopy using depth estimation, but a fundamental challenge is the need for ground-truth depth data to train algorithms capable of quantifying depth in physical units (e.g., meters). In this study, 60,000 paired virtual endoscopy images and depth maps were created in Blender from 3D airway models built from computed tomography. A U-Net convolutional neural network was trained to predict the depth maps from the endoscopy images. Point clouds were reconstructed from the AI-generated depth maps using the Equisolid fisheye lens model, and airway perimeters were identified by intersecting a plane with the point cloud to estimate CSA. Nasopharyngeal CSA, a key metric in obstructive sleep apnea, was quantified using this AI-enabled approach with a median error of 5.3 \% relative to the 3D model ground-truth. This pilot study using synthetic data provides strong evidence for the feasibility of developing AI-enabled quantitative endoscopy for airway CSA measurement.

papers.title: LightHybridNet: A Lightweight Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Efficient Multi-Label Ophthalmic Disease Classification in Imbalanced Fundus Images
papers.summary: Eye diseases are a major global cause of blindness and vision impairment, highlighting the need for accurate and early diagnosis to prevent further deterioration. Despite advances in medical imaging, classifying retinal diseases from fundus images remains challenging due to the complexity and subtlety of visual features. This study aims to develop and validate LightHybridNet, a novel lightweight hybrid deep learning framework, to improve the classification of eye diseases from fundus images. The model incorporates architectural features, such as depthwise separable convolutions and compound scaling mechanisms, to enhance diagnostic accuracy and robustness. To validate the model, the ODIR-5K dataset, comprising 8 disease categories, was used. To enhance image quality, pre-processing approaches were applied, including histogram equalisation, colour space conversion, and contrast adjustment, resulting in high-resolution images. Furthermore, image augmentation was employed to increase the dataset size, thereby improving the model's ability to generalise during training. The hybrid architecture helps the model concentrate on relevant image regions while capturing and integrating details at different scales, significantly improving classification performance. To evaluate its effectiveness, the model was compared with transfer-learning models. The results show that LightHybridNet outperforms the baselines, achieving a weighted F1-score of 91.51%, a macro AUC of 98.26%, and a Cohen's Kappa of 90.14% on the validation set. Furthermore, model interpretability was enhanced using explainable AI methods, including Grad-CAM, to identify and emphasise features influencing the decision-making process. LightHybridNet represents a promising advancement in automated ocular disease detection, offering improved diagnostic reliability for clinical use.

papers.title: Optimal Demand Response-Based Energy Management for Campus Buildings with Battery Energy Storage Systems: A Case Study of the ELB Building
papers.summary: Buildings account for a significant portion of global electricity consumption, making demand response (DR) an effective strategy for reducing energy costs and improving grid flexibility. This paper presents an optimal energy management framework for a campus building that integrates demand response and battery energy storage systems (BESS) to minimize electricity costs while satisfying operational constraints and occupant comfort requirements. The proposed optimization model schedules building loads and battery charging/discharging based on time-varying electricity prices and building demand profiles. The framework is validated using the Engineering Laboratory Building (ELB) at the University of Michigan-Dearborn as a real-world case study. Four operating scenarios are investigated: (i) baseline operation, (ii) demand response without battery energy storage, (iii) battery energy storage, and (iv) demand response with battery energy storage. Simulation results demonstrate that demand alone reduces the building's electricity cost by approximately 12% compared with conventional operation. When battery energy storage is incorporated, the total electricity cost reduction increases to approximately 26%, highlighting the significant economic benefits of coordinated demand response and energy storage scheduling. The results demonstrate that integrating battery energy storage with demand response substantially enhances the operational flexibility of campus buildings and provides an effective solution for cost-effective and sustainable building energy management.

papers.title: A Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Multi-Stream Quickest Change Detection
papers.summary: A Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework is proposed for quickest change detection (QCD) where there are multiple experts, and each expert produces a sequence of statistics for change detection. A change is declared when a weighted sum of these statistics crosses a threshold. This framework is then applied to the problem of multi-stream QCD to obtain a family of powerful algorithms that outperform the best known algorithms in the literature. In the multi-stream QCD problem, a decision-maker observes multiple streams of observations. At the change point, the distribution of an unknown subset of the streams changes. The optimal algorithm based on a generalized likelihood ratio is computationally expensive. One of the most computationally and performance-efficient algorithms in the literature is the rank-weighted sum (RWS) scheme based on Shiryaev-Roberts statistics. It is shown in the paper that the MoE-based QCD algorithm for multi-stream data outperforms the RWS scheme. This is demonstrated through simulation results on real-valued Gaussian mean shift data and high-dimensional data from Gaussian--Bernoulli Restricted Boltzmann Machines (GB-RBMs).

papers.title: Range Ambiguity Identification and Elimination by Leveraging Temporal Broadening Effect for THz Sensing
papers.summary: High pulse repetition frequency (PRF) operation improves Doppler unambiguous sensing but reduces the maximum unambiguous range of a terahertz (THz) pulsed radar. Echoes from targets beyond this range can be incorrectly associated with subsequent transmitted pulses, causing the targets to appear at shorter ranges. This paper proposes a receiver-side framework that exploits the THz-specific temporal broadening effect as a distance-dependent signature to resolve range ambiguity. For each detected echo, the receiver applies broadening-matched filtering with references corresponding to candidate target ranges. The filter outputs are combined across pulses with Doppler compensation, and the largest normalised combined response identifies the ambiguity order needed to recover the true target range. The selected reference is then reused to reduce mismatch loss in subsequent range and velocity estimation. Simulations under known atmospheric conditions, with targets occupying distinct apparent-delay bins, demonstrate reliable range recovery beyond the conventional unambiguous interval. Range estimation errors conditioned on correct ambiguity-order identification, together with the reported velocity estimation errors, approach their corresponding derived Cram\'er--Rao bounds. The method preserves a fixed transmitted pulse shape, PRF, and sampling rate, at the expense of a higher signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio requirement for ambiguity identification relative to the evaluated diversity-based techniques.

papers.title: Congestion Price Uncertainty From Interconnection Queue by Monte Carlo Sampling
papers.summary: The generation interconnection queue adds discrete uncertainty to power grid congestion price estimates on the project planning timescale. The conventional approach to this uncertainty is to make an informed guess of the single or few most likely configurations of generators that interconnect. In this paper, we show that Monte Carlo sampling is a more effective alternative. Given an estimate of the joint probability distribution of generator interconnections, a small number of samples yields good estimates of the congestion distribution. Crucially, this problem is not about rare events, but rather about the expected congestion over the worst times of the year, which makes congestion a common outcome over the distribution of interconnection events. We give empirical results on a 2000-bus network, averaging price outcomes from security-constrained DCOPF over eight different loading scenarios. For each line and contingency of the network, we estimate the full distribution as well as mean price and probability of exceeding a price threshold. Single-point estimates are unreliable and can be misleading about whether a line is likely to be congested. Combining the top k probability configurations yields improved estimates; however, sampling the same number from a distribution gives a more robust result of similar accuracy, as well as error estimates. Including correlation in the distribution model introduces small changes, showing that standard Bernoulli distributions suffice in most cases. The sampling approach is also applicable to large-load interconnection and should be of interest for planning both generation and large-load projects.

papers.title: Probing Neural Audio Codecs with Speaker Traits and Speech Characteristics
papers.summary: Neural audio codecs are increasingly used for low-bitrate speech coding and serve as tokenizers for speech language models, yet it remains unclear how their codebook hierarchies encode speaker traits and speech characteristics. We systematically study 17 multi-codebook neural audio codecs across seven traits: sex, age, accent, voice quality, emotion, speech flow, and non-verbal sounds. For each codec, we reconstruct speech using partial codebooks and use machine listeners to compare trait predictions on each reconstruction. We measure prediction agreement with reweighted Cohen's \k{appa}, and define trait depth as a proxy for the codebook depth by which each trait is encoded and recoverable. Overall, sex has the shallowest trait depth, followed by speech flow, whereas voice quality and age group require deeper stacks; emotion, accent, and non-verbal sounds fall in between. Within each trait, speech-flow classes are at relatively similar trait depths, whereas emotion, accent, and non-verbal sounds differ more. Additionally, we explore how certain codec design choices relate to trait depths. These findings show that codebook hierarchies are trait-dependent and may not exhibit uniform coarse-to-fine structures, motivating trait-specific codec evaluation and design for future applications.

papers.title: Integer-Free Control Synthesis for Signal Temporal Logic via Ranked Implicants
papers.summary: This paper proposes an integer-free method for control synthesis of nonlinear discrete-time systems under finite-horizon Signal Temporal Logic (STL) constraints. Instead of introducing integer variables, we consider the discrete choices of the specification in a ranked order and solve a standard nonlinear program for each selected choice until a satisfying trajectory is found. We first define implicants as sets of timed atomic constraints whose joint satisfaction is sufficient to satisfy the specification. A reference trajectory obtained from a smooth approximation of the STL robustness is used to rank these implicants. Fixing one implicant turns the problem into a standard nonlinear program with no auxiliary weights or bilinear terms. If the solution does not satisfy the specification, the next implicant will be considered. We prove soundness and completeness of our method relative to the nonlinear programming solver. Numerical evaluation on nonlinear multi-agent systems shows that our proposed method identifies satisfying trajectories where the exact continuous reformulation fails, and moreover, it is faster than a mixed-integer formulation of the same specification.

papers.title: Evidence Field for Histopathology: Cross-Centre Evaluation and Replayable Spatial Decisions
papers.summary: Histopathology classifiers must transfer across acquisition sites while exposing evidence that can be checked independently. Evidence Field couples learned image measurements and spatial classification with a native covering-program record. We evaluate this architecture on all 455,954 released CAMELYON17-WILDS patches, using patient-separated source partitions and two held-out hospital centres. Eighteen from-scratch fits compare four Evidence Field objectives with residual convolutional and compact vision-transformer classifiers. Checkpoints, temperatures and review thresholds are selected using source validation. The source-selected paired-cross-entropy ensemble achieves areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.9356 and 0.9453, with accuracies of 84.46% and 86.77% at the two held-out centres. Corresponding convolutional values are 0.7352 and 0.7656, and transformer values are 0.8502 and 0.7924. Evidence Field has 10,550 trainable parameters per member and additionally returns selected covers, signed region and interaction terms, contextual dependencies and independently reconstructible predictions. Patient-cluster intervals, calibration, source-fixed review policies and recorded training resources characterize the results. A 340-image, three-member audit reconstructs probability mixtures and 6,120 class programs under three rigid views. The evaluation supports cross-centre discrimination and reproducible computation for these implemented models; unequal family tuning, previously examined public targets and limited patient groups constrain broader interpretation.

papers.title: VoxTurn: Answering Several Turn-Taking Questions in One Pass with One Model
papers.summary: A cascaded voice agent must decide, throughout each silence of its user, whether the user has finished their turn: answering too early cuts the user off, answering too late makes the agent slow. It often needs related decisions too: will the user soon go on, is speech during its own turn an interruption or a backchannel, is a sound speech at all. With open detectors, each extra decision costs another model or another call, and on the 14-language eot-bench they cut users off in more than a quarter of mid-turn pauses. Because they are trained on segmented utterances, this mismatch is the largest single source of error. We present VoxTurn, a 0.8B speech LLM that casts these decisions as multiple-choice questions, scores the hidden state of each option, and answers any set of them in one forward pass with a block-isolating attention mask, exactly as if asked one at a time. Trained on real conversational pauses with labels derived from their timing, and re-queried while a silence lasts, VoxTurn reaches 11.5% false cut-offs in English at a 300 ms latency budget, comparable to two commercial detectors, and a 14-language mean of 19.9%, the lowest among open models, at 8.3 ms per decision. In Pipecat and LiveKit it cuts off 17% and 9% of turns, and it ranks fifth of 24 in TurnBench end-of-turn detection without any TurnBench training data. The model, code and framework plugins are released.

papers.title: Tokenized Joint Source-Network Coding for Loss-Resilient Video Streaming
papers.summary: For decades, conventional video streaming systems have relied on packet-level forward error correction (FEC) codes and retransmissions to ensure reliable video delivery. However, in real-time communications, FEC is inherently inefficient under unknown and time-varying packet-loss conditions, while retransmission can incur excessive latency and fail to meet stringent playout deadlines. Emerging deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) provides an alternative by learning channel-noise-resilient representations, yet its tight coupling with the physical layer makes it difficult to integrate into today's layered network architectures and protocols. In this paper, we propose TokJSNC, a simple-but-effective tokenized joint source-network coding paradigm for packet-loss-resilient video streaming. Rather than first compressing video into a compact bitstream and then protecting it with packet-level FEC, TokJSNC directly encodes video into variable-length discrete token-stream, whose transmission rate is jointly adapted to video content complexity and network conditions. By exploiting the spatiotemporal correlations among learned video tokens, TokJSNC enables robust video reconstruction over a wide range of packet-loss rates without explicit FEC or retransmissions. Consequently, TokJSNC brings the JSCC-like graceful degradation property to the network layer while remaining compatible with existing network architectures and transport protocols. Experimental results show that TokJSNC maintains an average playback frame rate above 22 fps even at a 70% packet-loss rate, whereas the best-performing baseline drops below 12 fps. Overall, TokJSNC establishes a practical pathway for repurposing modern generative video tokenizers for loss-resilient streaming, while providing a fundamental framework for video token communications.

papers.title: Physical AI: A Survey of Models, Learning, Systems, and Open Challenges
papers.summary: Physical AI aims to enable intelligent systems to perceive, reason, act, and learn through interaction with the physical world. Unlike purely digital intelligence, physical agents must operate under partial observability, uncertain dynamics, embodiment constraints, and real-time requirements, while their actions continuously reshape the environment and subsequent observations. Recent advances in foundation models and robot learning have expanded the capabilities of physical agents, yet achieving reliable autonomy requires more than improvements in individual models. This survey presents a comprehensive, system-level review of Physical AI, organized around the closed-loop process of physical interaction. We examine the foundations and recent developments in task representations and memory, predictive and action-generating models, data and learning methods, embodiment and control, computing systems, evaluation, and safety. Beyond reviewing individual advances, we investigate how these components interact and collectively shape the capabilities and limitations of Physical AI systems. Building on this integrated perspective, we identify fundamental challenges in generalization, resource-efficient learning and execution, reliable state tracking, safety, recovery, and continual adaptation. We argue that advancing Physical AI requires moving beyond isolated model performance toward integrated systems capable of robust, efficient, safe, and autonomous physical interaction under changing real-world conditions.

papers.title: Antenna Placement for Movable Antenna-Enabled Near-Field Target Localization
papers.summary: Movable antennas (MAs) have recently emerged as a promising technology to enhance the wireless sensing performance by exploiting additional spatial degrees of freedom. In this work, we consider an MA-enabled near-field target localization problem under a device-based sensing architecture, where the sensing target actively transmits signals and the sensing receiver estimates its location based on the received signals. We adopt the squared position error bound (SPEB) as the sensing performance metric and aim to minimize the target's SPEB by optimizing the antenna placement at the sensing receiver. The resulting optimization problem is highly non-convex due to the minimum antenna spacing constraints and the intricate dependence of the SPEB on the antenna locations and the intractable form of SPEB. To tackle this problem, we first relax the inter-spacing constraints and accordingly formulate an antenna position distribution problem in terms of degree-4 truncated moments. The reformulated moment-based problem admits an equivalent semidefinite programming formulation and can be optimally solved using standard convex optimization solvers. Using truncated moment theory, we then recover an optimal antenna position distribution supported on a finite number of locations and construct an efficient clustered placement policy. Numerical results demonstrate that the constructed optimal distribution exhibits a three-cluster structure with source-dependent weights. The proposed antenna placement method outperforms conventional array geometries and closely approaches the exhaustive-search benchmark scheme.
