papers.title: Denoising Rather Than Gap Filling: Missing-Data Handling in Sparse Outdoor BLE Positioning
papers.summary: Received signal strength indicator (RSSI) positioning outdoors has one to two orders of magnitude fewer anchors than the indoor systems its methods come from. In the ten-day cattle-tracking deployment reported here, four gateways cover $4{,}302\,\mathrm{m}^2$, or $0.93$ anchors per $1000\,\mathrm{m}^2$. An animal is heard by $0.99$ gateways per second on average, so the observation vector for a given second is almost never complete. How the gaps are filled is therefore a first-order design choice, not a preprocessing detail. Filling at all is worth $8.1\,\mathrm{m}$, $96\%$ of the improvement the hold-length setting can deliver and a $29\%$ error reduction. How long a value is then held is worth the remaining $4\%$, from four seconds to unbounded. Once a value is available, the gain comes from removing noise rather than rebuilding the lost sample: a filtered channel estimate improves on a held raw sample, whereas filling backwards from future samples makes it worse. As that mechanism predicts, smoothing strength has a real interior optimum that is costly to miss in either direction. A smoother allowed to read the future gains only $0.55\,\mathrm{m}$, one fifteenth of what filling is worth, which bounds what any offline method can add. Three method families do not apply here for structural reasons rather than poor performance: two or more of the four channels are live in only $25\%$ of seconds, so the cross-channel structure generative imputation must learn is largely unobserved.

papers.title: Centroid Angle Estimation of Multiple Scatterers Using Monopulse Radar with Frequency Diversity
papers.summary: The monopulse technique determines the angle of a target by comparing signals from two narrow beams, yielding a precise angular estimate with low complexity. However, it struggles to resolve multiple closely spaced scatterers within the same resolution cell. Existing methods for estimating multiple scatterer angles involve complex signal processing and system modifications. We propose an effective method to estimate the angular centroid of scatterers using the mode of monopulse angle estimates. A semi-analytic expression for the angle estimate distribution is derived, confirming that its mode aligns with the centroid. To enhance estimation accuracy, we employ frequency diversity to reduce sample correlation. Numerical results validate the advantages of the proposed method, demonstrating superior performance over conventional techniques with low complexity.

papers.title: A Deficiency-Based Approach for Unbalanced Three-Phase Distribution System Expansion Planning
papers.summary: Distribution planners typically characterize grid needs through power flow studies and fit upgrades to those needs by hand. More principled one-shot optimization methods either do not scale or misrepresent unbalanced three-phase networks. This paper proposes an iterative planning process that alternates between two problem classes with mature off-the-shelf solvers. An optimal power flow (OPF) problem quantifies the deficiency of a candidate portfolio by optimizing the dispatch of controllable devices and measuring thermal and voltage violations on a common scale, with an optimal value of zero exactly at adequate portfolios. The OPF multipliers give a first-order approximation of the relief each investment candidate would provide. We bound the error of this approximation and show that structural properties of the deficiency guard it against overestimation. Building on this property, a heuristic cutting-plane search uses a mixed-integer linear program to propose each next portfolio from these approximations. On six unbalanced three-phase feeders from the SMART-DS dataset, the search outperforms a linearized optimization-based benchmark, and the results agree across five variants of the deficiency.

papers.title: Sensing-Aided Vehicular Beam Tracking: System Gain Over Link Feedback and Probe-Verified Sensing Invocation
papers.summary: Sensor-based beam prediction is usually evaluated against exhaustive beam training, leaving open when sensing adds useful information beyond a deployed tracker's link feedback and when it should be withheld. We separate system gain from the marginal value of sensing in action-restricted causal replay of recorded 64-beam sweeps from four vehicular DeepSense 6G scenarios. The replay exposes only serving-beam and explicitly probed candidate powers and counts probes and model invocations separately. The proposed controller combines a scheduled post-setup re-sweep with probe-verified sensing admission and blacklist backoff. In three scenarios where feedback-only tracking is within 0.25 dB of the recorded-sweep oracle, the controller stays close to feedback-only in mean loss while rarely invoking the model, whereas always-on sensing performs worse. In the sole high-innovation scenario, the controller's system gain is 0.82 dB (95% confidence interval [0.30, 1.40]) over the plain feedback-only tracker and 0.15 dB over a probe-limited re-sweeping reference, with fewer probes than either. Sensing and the re-sweep both correct setup lock loss. At the native decision interval, enabling sensing in the same controller yields no statistically resolved loss reduction but cuts probing by 21%. In this scenario, accurate sensing reduces loss relative to the sensor-disabled controller under emulated link noise, staleness or longer decision intervals. Weak or delayed sensing can instead increase loss despite probe verification. These exploratory results characterize sensing as a conditional substitute for RF probing or a source of loss reduction, depending on the limitations of link feedback and on the accuracy and timeliness of sensing.

papers.title: Modeling Diffuse Scattering in Mobility Scenarios: Ray Tracing Model and Measurement Validation
papers.summary: Open-source ray tracing (RT) frameworks are increasingly used for site-specific channel modeling due to their reproducibility and extensibility. In non-stationary mobility scenarios, repeated RT evaluations can generate different diffuse propagation paths without preserving their correspondence, limiting a consistent representation of their temporal evolution. To address this limitation, we extend diffuse scattering modeling in Sionna RT using persistent surface-associated scattering points. Their positions remain fixed, while their contributions evolve according to changes in the propagation geometry and visibility. The proposed approach is validated using empirical radio channel impulse response measurements in an urban vehicular scenario at 5.9 GHz. Compared with the standard Sionna RT baseline, the proposed model shows improved agreement with measurements in the delay and Doppler domains.

papers.title: Z-Opt: A Near-Optimal Reduced-Complexity Two-Dimensional Grassmannian Constellation
papers.summary: Grassmannian constellations achieve the capacity of noncoherent communications over Rayleigh fading channels at high SNR, yet their efficient construction remains challenging. In this paper, we present two construction methods for Grassmannian constellations on G(2,1), termed S-Opt and Z-Opt, and propose two low-complexity detectors. Both construction and detection are performed on the unit sphere, known as the Bloch sphere in quantum computing. Exploiting the proportionality between the chordal distance on the Grassmann manifold and the Euclidean distance on the Bloch sphere, we derive a theoretical upper bound on the minimum chordal distance from the Fejes-Toth bound. The S-Opt constellation is constructed from sphere-packing solutions and achieves the theoretical limit corresponding to the considered optimal Bloch-sphere packings. The S-Opt detector applies to arbitrary constellations on G(2,1) and requires a number of complex multiplications scaling linearly with the number of receive antennas and logarithmically with the constellation size, and a number of numerical comparisons scaling logarithmically with the constellation size, while achieving the same performance as the GLRT detector. Based on the insight from the S-Opt construction, we further propose the Z-Opt constellation, constructed by stacking regular polygons on the Bloch sphere, whose minimum chordal distance approaches the derived upper bound over the evaluated constellation sizes. The Z-Opt detector requires a number of complex multiplications scaling linearly with the number of receive antennas and a number of numerical comparisons scaling logarithmically with the square root of the constellation size, while achieving the same performance as the GLRT detector for the Z-Opt constellation.

papers.title: A Unified Two-Stage Generative Diffusion Framework for Channel Estimation and Port Selection in Multiuser MIMO-FAS
papers.summary: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) have emerged as a promising technology for next-generation wireless systems. However, practical multiuser multiple-input multiple-output FAS (MIMO-FAS) faces two inherently coupled challenges: acquiring accurate high-dimensional channel state information (CSI) from limited RF chains and solving the combinatorial port selection problem, where the effectiveness of the latter highly depends on the result of the former. In this paper, we propose a unified two-stage diffusion framework that formulates the joint task as a maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) inference problem equivalent to maximizing the posterior expected utility of the port selection, and approximates it through two sequential stages. For Stage I, we employ a continuous flow-based diffusion model as a powerful implicit prior for 2D FAS channels and perform approximate posterior sampling via a parallel guided generation scheme, enabling accurate multiuser channel recovery even under severely low sub-sampling ratios. For Stage II, we train a discrete diffusion model on optimal labels computed by exhaustive search to propose a pool of promising port selection candidates. The final selection is then determined by maximizing the empirical posterior expected utility over this pool, followed by a lightweight local refinement. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed framework simultaneously achieves accurate channel estimation and delivers over 90% of the deployed rate of the computationally expensive exhaustive search over the estimated channel, while substantially improving the minimum achievable rate relative to practical cascaded schemes.

papers.title: Geometry-Aware Control Barrier Functions for Collision Avoidance via Bernstein Polynomial Approximations
papers.summary: Safe navigation often relies on well-defined conditions based on the shape of robots and obstacles, and can be challenging when they have irregular geometries. While Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) offer an efficient mechanism to enforce safe set forward invariance, common shape surrogates (e.g., spheres or super-ellipsoids) are either overly conservative in unstructured scenes or require many local primitives, which inflates constraint counts and degrades real-time performance. In this paper, we introduce a novel geometry-aware Control Barrier Function (CBF) based on Bernstein-Polynomial Signed Distance Fields (BP-SDFs). It provides a unified way to represent the obstacles and robots, so as to represent the barrier function with a unified minimum distance. Benefiting from the differentiability of the Bernstein polynomials, one can easily enforce the control constraints in a closed loop. We validate the method's efficiency and performance to guarantee safety in single-robot navigation and heterogeneous multi-robot collision avoidance via simulations under different environments.

papers.title: Smooth Hard-Thresholding for Singular Values with Stein's Unbiased Risk Estimate
papers.summary: Low-rank matrix denoising is a central primitive in patch-based image restoration and many other inverse problems. Classical SVD-based image denoising methods often choose a truncation rank by matching residual singular-value energy with an estimated noise energy, but this rule is not a finite-sample risk principle because a fitted low-rank approximation inevitably absorbs part of the noise. This paper develops a mathematically rigorous alternative based on Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE). Since singular value hard thresholding is discontinuous and does not satisfy the hypotheses of Stein's lemma, we introduce a logistic smooth hard-threshold spectral estimator. We prove that the smooth shrinker satisfies the regularity conditions required by a spectral-estimator version of Stein's lemma, and therefore admits an exactly unbiased fixed-threshold risk estimate under Gaussian noise. For a fixed observed matrix and a finite set of candidate thresholds separated from the observed singular values, the ordering of the fixed-threshold smooth SURE objective eventually agrees with a simple limiting score. The limiting score has the same algebraic form as the biased hard-threshold SURE formula, but here it is used only as a computational device for ranking finite candidates. Selecting the minimizing threshold is a data-adaptive tuning step; the selected SURE value should not be interpreted as an unbiased risk estimate of the finally selected estimator.

papers.title: The MPB Corpus: A Dataset of Melody, Rhythm, Harmony, and Melody-Harmony Relationships in Brazilian Popular Music
papers.summary: PLEASE CHECK AND REFER TO THE PUBLISHED VERSION OF THIS PAPER ON https://doi.org/10.5334/tismir.357 This paper presents the MPB Corpus, a dataset of Brazilian Popular Music (Musica Popular Brasileira, MPB) comprising derived symbolic annotations for 500 pieces across four musical parameters -- melodic contour, melodic rhythm, harmony, and the melody-harmony relationship -- making it the most comprehensive dataset to date for computational musicology of Brazilian music. It is released under a CC-BY-4.0 license in an open, machine-readable tabular format, with documentation and reproducible analysis code. Because the annotations were derived from copyrighted musical scores, the corpus contains no audio recordings or score-level representations such as MIDI or MusicXML; it nonetheless provides a reusable resource for MIR research on a culturally significant repertoire that remains underrepresented in existing datasets. To support the encoding process, we introduce analytical models for capturing rhythmic and melodic information, along with tailored visualizations and summary metrics. Finally, we present a brief exploratory analysis illustrating the dataset's potential for formulating and addressing musicological questions about the genre.
